journeys.title: 1 &  2 Corinthians: A Church Shaped by Jesus
journeys.subtitle: Following Jesus through division, difficulty and change
journeys.description:
The church in Corinth had spiritual gifts, passionate worship and great potential.

It also struggled with division, immorality, pride, disorder and false teaching.

In these two letters, Paul brings the believers back to the Cross, calls them to honour God with their bodies, teaches them to use spiritual gifts in love and shows them how the power of Jesus is revealed through human weakness.

metadata.completionMessage: Corinthians complete. Stay devoted to Jesus, walk in love and trust His strength in your weakness.
metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to 1 and 2 Corinthians.

Corinth was a wealthy, influential and deeply immoral city.

Its culture celebrated status, persuasive speech, personal freedom and physical desire.

Although the believers had come to Jesus, many of the city’s values had followed them into the Church.

They compared leaders.

They tolerated serious sin.

They misused their freedom.

They competed over spiritual gifts.

They questioned the Resurrection.

And later, some were drawn towards leaders who appeared more impressive than Paul.

It would have been easy to give up on this church.

Paul did not.

He corrected them because he loved them and wanted them to return to sincere devotion to Jesus.

He reminded them that the Church belongs to Christ.

Jesus alone was crucified for them.

Their bodies belonged to Him.

Their spiritual gifts came from the Holy Spirit.

Their gatherings were meant to strengthen others.

Their leadership had to reflect the character of Jesus.

And everything they did needed to be governed by love.

These letters also show us that Christian ministry does not depend upon appearing powerful or impressive.

God places His treasure in fragile people so that everyone can see that the power comes from Him.

His grace is sufficient.

His strength is revealed through weakness.

As you begin this Walk, invite the Holy Spirit to examine your heart.

Allow Jesus to confront pride, compromise, comparison and self-reliance.

And ask Him to shape your life through the Cross, His love and the hope of the Resurrection.

journeys.title: 1 and 2 Thessalonians: Walking and Waiting
journeys.subtitle: Living faithfully while we wait for Jesus to return
journeys.description:
The believers in Thessalonica were young in their faith and facing intense opposition.

Paul encourages them to keep walking with Jesus in holiness, love and faithful service while they wait with hope for His return.

This Walk explores faith, love, hope, Christian character, Resurrection, the Second Coming and remaining faithful in ordinary life.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to 1 and 2 Thessalonians.

Paul spent only a short time in Thessalonica before opposition forced him to leave.

The new believers were left in a hostile environment with limited teaching and little experience.

Paul feared that persecution might overwhelm them.

Instead, he received encouraging news.

Their faith was growing.

Their love was increasing.

Their hope in Jesus was helping them endure.

They had turned from idols to serve the living God and wait for His Son to return from Heaven.

But they still needed guidance.

They had questions about believers who had died.

They were confused about the timing of Jesus’ return.

Some became so focused on the Second Coming that they neglected their ordinary responsibilities.

Paul brings them back to a balanced Christian life.

We walk with Jesus.

And we wait for Jesus.

Walking means growing in holiness, loving others, working faithfully, praying continually and remaining responsive to the Holy Spirit.

Waiting means living with the confident hope that Jesus will return, the dead will be raised and God will bring perfect justice.

Waiting for Jesus is not an excuse to withdraw from life.

It gives us a reason to live faithfully now.

As you begin this Walk, ask the Holy Spirit to strengthen your faith, deepen your love and renew your hope.

Keep walking in holiness.

Keep serving faithfully.

And keep waiting expectantly for Jesus.

journeys.title: 1 and 2 Timothy: Guard the Truth
journeys.subtitle: Living faithfully and passing the Gospel to others
journeys.description:
Paul’s letters to Timothy reveal how believers can remain faithful in a world of false teaching, spiritual confusion and increasing opposition.

This Walk explores sound teaching, godly character, Christian leadership, courage, endurance and the importance of passing the Gospel faithfully to others.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to 1 and 2 Timothy.

Timothy was a younger leader with a demanding responsibility.

Paul had left him in Ephesus to care for the church, confront false teaching and help God’s people live faithfully.

Timothy faced pressure from within the church and opposition from outside it. He also carried personal fears and insecurities.

Paul writes to strengthen him.

First Timothy focuses on life within God’s Household.

The church must remain grounded in the truth, committed to prayer and shaped by godly leadership. Those who lead must be recognised not only by their ability, but also by their character.

Second Timothy is Paul’s final letter.

Paul is imprisoned and approaching the end of his life. Many people have abandoned him, yet his confidence in Jesus remains unshaken.

He urges Timothy not to become ashamed or afraid.

The Holy Spirit gives power, love and self-discipline.

The Gospel must be guarded, lived and entrusted to faithful people who will pass it to others.

These letters remind us that truth and character belong together.

Sound teaching should produce love, godliness, courage, generosity and faithful service.

Following Jesus will not always be easy. There may be opposition, disappointment and loneliness.

Yet the Lord remains faithful.

He stands with His people and gives them strength.

As you begin this Walk, ask the Holy Spirit to deepen your understanding of Scripture, strengthen your character and help you remain faithful to Jesus.

Guard the truth.

Live the Gospel.

Pass it faithfully to others.

And keep going until you finish the race.

journeys.title: 10 Minutes with Jesus
journeys.description: A short, guided journey to help you connect with Jesus in the middle of your everyday life.

journeys.title: Acts: The Church on the Move
journeys.subtitle: The continuing work of Jesus through the power of the Holy Spirit
journeys.description:
Acts begins with the risen Jesus preparing His disciples to become His witnesses.

It follows the Good News from Jerusalem into Judaea and Samaria, across cultural boundaries and eventually to Rome.

Along the way, frightened disciples become courageous witnesses, divided people become one Church and ordinary believers are empowered by the Holy Spirit.

Acts shows us that the mission of Jesus did not end with His Ascension.

Jesus continues His work through His Church.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to the book of Acts.
The Gospel of Luke records what Jesus began to do and teach.
Acts shows us what Jesus continued to do through His followers after He returned to Heaven.
The disciples could not fulfil this calling through their own strength.
They needed the Holy Spirit.
When the Holy Spirit came upon them, everything changed.
Fear became courage.
Silence became witness.
A small group of believers became a growing Church.
The Good News moved from Jerusalem into Judaea and Samaria, then across nations and cultures until it reached Rome.
Nothing could stop it.
Not persecution.
Not imprisonment.
Not cultural division.
Not distance.
Not even the failures and disagreements within the Church.
Acts does not present a perfect group of people.
It presents a faithful God working through ordinary people who depend upon Him.
Throughout this Walk, you will see the Kingdom of God proclaimed, the name of Jesus lifted up and the power of the Holy Spirit transforming lives.
The story of Acts is not merely a record of what God did long ago.
Jesus is still building His Church.
The Holy Spirit is still empowering His people.
The Gospel is still crossing boundaries.
And the mission is still continuing.
Ask the Holy Spirit to open your heart as you begin.
You are not only reading the story.
You have been invited to become part of it.

journeys.title: Beginning Your New Life
journeys.description: Discover what it means to begin a new life with Jesus, grow in your relationship with Him, and take your first steps as His follower.

metadata.introductionContent:
You've discovered what Jesus has done for you.

He came to us.

He took our sin upon Himself at the Cross.

He died.

He rose again.

And He offers us forgiveness and new life as a gift.

But what happens when you say yes to Jesus?

Is that the end?

Not at all.

It's the beginning.

Following Jesus doesn't mean that every problem suddenly disappears.

It doesn't mean you'll never struggle again.

It doesn't mean you'll understand everything about God tomorrow.

And it certainly doesn't mean you have to become a perfect Christian overnight.

Something new has begun.

The Bible describes coming to Jesus as new life.

You begin discovering who you are because of Him.

You begin learning to recognise God's Presence in your everyday life.

You begin opening Scripture differently—not simply to learn information, but to know the God who speaks through it.

You begin talking to God.

You discover that you aren't meant to follow Jesus alone.

And gradually, you learn what it means to follow Him in the ordinary moments of your life.

There will be questions.

There will be things you don't understand.

There may even be times when you stumble.

Keep walking.

Jesus didn't invite you to have everything figured out before following Him.

He simply said:

"Follow Me."

Over the next few steps, we'll begin discovering what that new life with Jesus looks like.

Your journey with Him is just beginning.

journeys.title: Colossians: Jesus Is Enough
journeys.subtitle: Rooted in Christ and transformed by His Life
journeys.description:
Colossians reveals the supremacy and complete sufficiency of Jesus.

Paul warns believers against mixing faith in Christ with spiritual ideas, religious rules and practices that draw attention away from Him.

This three-day Walk explores who Jesus is, the fullness we receive in Him and the new life that must become visible in our character and relationships.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to Colossians.

The believers in Colosse lived among many competing spiritual beliefs.

Some people feared invisible powers.

Others looked to astrology, angels, secret knowledge or religious rituals for spiritual security.

These ideas began entering the Church.

The believers had not completely abandoned Jesus.

But they were in danger of treating Him as one spiritual power among many.

Paul brings them back to the centre.

Jesus is the visible Image of the invisible God.

Everything was created through Him and for Him.

He existed before all things.

Everything is held together in Him.

He is the Head of the Church.

And all the fullness of God lives in Him.

Nothing needs to be added to Jesus.

Through the Cross, He has forgiven our sins, cancelled our debt and defeated the powers that held us in fear.

Those who belong to Him have been made alive and brought to fullness in Him.

But new life in Jesus must become visible.

We put off the attitudes and behaviours of the old life.

We put on compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience and love.

The Lordship of Jesus begins shaping our homes, work, speech and relationships.

As you begin this Walk, bring every competing fear, belief and source of security before Jesus.

Remain rooted in Him.

Allow His Word to dwell richly within you.

And trust that everything you need for life with God is found in Christ.

Jesus is enough.

journeys.title: Created in God's Image
journeys.description: Discover what it means to be created by God, made in His image, and given dignity, purpose and a place in His creation.

metadata.completionMessage: You were created by God, made in His image and given purpose and value. Now let's discover what happened to God's good creation—and why we need Him to restore what has been broken.
metadata.introductionContent:
You are not an accident.

The Bible says that when God created humanity, He did something unique.

He created us **in His image**.

That doesn't mean we look physically like God. It means there is something about human beings that reflects the God who created us.

That truth changes the way we understand ourselves.

Your value isn't determined by what you own, what you've achieved, what other people think about you, or even what you think about yourself.

Your story begins somewhere deeper.

**You were created by God.**

Over the next few steps, we're going to explore what it means to be made in God's image, why God created us, the purpose He gave humanity, and what this tells us about the value of every human life.

We'll also discover that we were never created to live disconnected from God or from one another.

God created us for relationship.

He created us with purpose.

And He created us to reflect something of who He is.

Before we explore what went wrong with humanity, it's important that we first understand what God intended from the beginning.

So let's go back to the moment when God created humanity and said,

"Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness..."

Your story begins there.

journeys.title: Ephesians: Alive in Christ
journeys.subtitle: Discovering who we are in Jesus and how He calls us to live
journeys.description:
Ephesians reveals God’s purpose to bring everything together under Jesus Christ.

Paul explains how we are saved by grace, made alive with Jesus and brought into one new family through the Cross.

This Walk moves from our identity in Christ to our daily walk with Him through unity, maturity, love, relationships and spiritual warfare.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to Ephesians.

Ephesians can be understood in two clear parts.

The first half explains what God has done for us in Christ.

The second half shows how we should live because of what He has done.

The order matters.

Christianity does not begin with trying to become good enough for God.

We are not saved by good works.

We are saved by grace through faith in Jesus.

Then God begins transforming us so that we can walk in the good works He has prepared for us.

Christian behaviour grows from Christian belief.

Our duty flows from our identity.

In Jesus, we have been chosen, adopted, redeemed and forgiven.

We have been made alive.

We have been brought near to God.

We have received the Holy Spirit.

And we have become part of one family with every other believer.

The Cross has broken down the barriers that separated us from God and from one another.

Now we are called to walk in a way that reflects this new life.

To walk in humility.

To protect unity.

To grow towards maturity.

To speak the truth in love.

To live in purity.

To keep being filled with the Holy Spirit.

To serve faithfully in our closest relationships.

And to stand firm when spiritual opposition comes.

As you begin this Walk, ask the Holy Spirit to open the eyes of your heart.

Receive what God has given you in Jesus.

Then allow that truth to reshape every part of the way you live.

journeys.title: Galatians: Free in Christ
journeys.subtitle: Living by faith through the power of the Holy Spirit
journeys.description:
Galatians protects the heart of the Gospel.

Paul confronts teachers who claimed that faith in Jesus was not enough and that believers also needed to keep the Law of Moses to be accepted by God.

This Walk explores justification by faith, our identity as God’s children, freedom in Christ, life in the Holy Spirit and the call to carry one another’s burdens.

metadata.completionMessage: Galatians complete. Stand firm in the freedom of Jesus and keep in step with the Holy Spirit.
metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to Galatians.

The believers in Galatia had received the Good News of Jesus.

They had begun their new lives through faith.

They had received the Holy Spirit.

Then other teachers arrived and told them that Jesus was not enough.

They needed Jesus plus circumcision.

Jesus plus the Law of Moses.

Jesus plus religious achievement.

Paul knew this was not a small disagreement.

Adding anything as a requirement for acceptance with God changes the Gospel itself.

We cannot make ourselves right with God by keeping religious rules.

We are justified through faith in Jesus Christ.

He loved us and gave Himself for us.

At the Cross, Jesus carried the curse of sin and opened the way for us to become children of God.

But freedom from the Law does not mean freedom to live however we please.

Jesus sets us free from religious slavery and from the rule of sin.

The Holy Spirit leads us into a new way of life.

He forms the character of Jesus within us.

He teaches us to love, serve, restore and carry one another’s burdens.

Galatians calls us away from two dangers.

Trying to earn God’s acceptance through human effort.

And using grace as an excuse for compromise.

The answer to both is the same.

Faith in Jesus.

Dependence upon the Holy Spirit.

And a life shaped by the Cross.

As you begin this Walk, release the pressure to prove yourself to God.

Stand firmly in the freedom Jesus has given you.

And invite the Holy Spirit to lead every step you take.

journeys.title: Jesus Saves
journeys.description: Discover who Jesus is, why He came, what happened at the Cross, why the resurrection matters, and how His saving work changes everything.

metadata.introductionContent:
Everything we've discovered so far has been leading here.

God created humanity in His image.

He created us with purpose, value and the opportunity to know Him.

But humanity turned away from God.

And we discovered something difficult:

We cannot repair what sin has broken by ourselves.

We need to be rescued.

The good news of Christianity is that God didn't wait for us to find a way back to Him.

He came to us.

Jesus stands at the centre of the Christian faith.

He wasn't simply a wise teacher who gave humanity better ideas about how to live.

He didn't come merely to start another religion.

Jesus came because we needed something we could never accomplish for ourselves.

He came to save us.

Over the next few steps, we're going to discover who Jesus really is, why He came, what happened when He died on the cross, why His resurrection changes everything, and what all of this means for you.

Some of these truths may be familiar.

Others may be completely new.

Either way, don't rush through them.

Because the message of Jesus isn't simply information to understand.

Eventually it asks every one of us a deeply personal question:

What will I do with Jesus?

We ended the previous Walk with a simple truth:

We needed a Rescuer.

Now we're going to meet Him.

His Name is Jesus.

journeys.title: Luke
journeys.subtitle: Discovering Jesus through the careful, compassionate account of Luke
journeys.description:
Luke presents Jesus as the Saviour who came for all people.

Writing as a doctor, historian, traveller and companion of Paul, Luke carefully investigated the events surrounding Jesus’ life. He wanted his reader to have confidence that the Christian faith rested on real events and reliable testimony.

Luke pays particular attention to people who were often overlooked: Samaritans, Gentiles, women, the poor, social outcasts and those known simply as “sinners.”

Throughout his Gospel, we encounter the Holy Spirit, prayer, joy, compassion, forgiveness and salvation.

This five-day Walk follows the major movements of Luke’s Gospel and helps us see Jesus as the One who came to seek and save the lost.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to the Gospel of Luke.

Some of the most loved stories about Jesus are found only here.

The Good Samaritan.

The lost son welcomed home.

Zacchaeus in the tree.

The dying thief.

The two disciples on the road to Emmaus.

Luke gathered these stories carefully. He spoke with eyewitnesses, investigated what had happened and arranged his account so that his reader could know the certainty of what he had been taught.

But Luke was doing more than recording history.

He wanted us to meet Jesus.

Jesus welcomes the outsider.

Jesus touches the powerless.

Jesus forgives sinners.

Jesus seeks those who are lost.

Jesus is the Saviour of the world.

As you begin this Walk, ask the Holy Spirit to help you see Jesus more clearly and follow Him more faithfully.

journeys.title: Philippians: Joy in Jesus
journeys.subtitle: Living with humility, purpose and contentment in every circumstance
journeys.description:
Paul wrote Philippians from prison, yet his letter is filled with joy.

His joy did not depend upon freedom, comfort or favourable circumstances. It came from knowing Jesus, sharing in the Gospel and trusting God’s purpose.

This three-day Walk explores Gospel partnership, the humility of Jesus and the call to press forward with peace and contentment.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to Philippians.

Paul wrote this letter while under house arrest in Rome.

His movement was restricted.

His future was uncertain.

His circumstances were difficult.

Yet he continued to rejoice.

Paul’s joy was rooted in Jesus.

He could see God working through his imprisonment.

He valued the faithful partnership of the Philippian church.

And he trusted that whether he lived or died, Jesus would remain his greatest treasure.

Philippians shows us that joy is deeper than happiness.

Happiness changes with our circumstances.

Joy grows from knowing Jesus and living for something that hardship cannot destroy.

This letter also calls us towards humility.

Jesus possessed the very nature of God, yet He chose the position of a servant and became obedient to death on the Cross.

His attitude must now shape our relationships.

Following Jesus means releasing pride, selfish ambition and the need for recognition.

It means allowing God to work within us and then working out that salvation through daily obedience.

Philippians also calls us to keep moving forward.

We cannot become right with God through our achievements.

Our righteousness comes through faith in Jesus.

Knowing Him is worth more than everything else.

As you begin this Walk, ask the Holy Spirit to deepen your joy in Jesus.

Allow Him to confront pride and anxiety.

And trust Him to give you strength to remain faithful in every circumstance.

journeys.title: Romans
journeys.subtitle: Romans: One Gospel, One Family
journeys.description:
Romans explains how guilty people can be made right with a Holy God.

Paul shows that everyone has sinned, salvation is received through faith and new life is made possible by the Holy Spirit.

The Gospel removes our pride, restores our relationship with God and brings people from different backgrounds together as one family in Jesus.

metadata.introductionContent:
Welcome to Romans.

Romans is Paul’s longest letter.

He wrote to believers in Rome from both Jewish and Gentile backgrounds.

Although they followed the same Jesus, their different histories, traditions and convictions were creating tension between them.

Some were tempted to feel spiritually superior.

Others were judging people who lived differently from them.

Paul brings everyone back to the Gospel.

All have sinned.

No one can make themselves right with God.

No one can boast.

God offers forgiveness and righteousness freely through faith in Jesus Christ.

But salvation is more than receiving forgiveness.

Jesus sets us free from sin’s penalty.

The Holy Spirit begins setting us free from sin’s power.

And one day, God will set us free completely from sin’s presence.

Romans shows us how grace changes everything.

It changes our relationship with God.

It changes the way we understand ourselves.

It changes the way we respond to sin.

It changes the way we see people from different backgrounds.

And it changes the way we live together as the Church.

As you begin this Walk, come honestly before God.

Leave behind comparison, pride and self-reliance.

Ask the Holy Spirit to help you understand the Gospel more deeply and live in the freedom Jesus has given you.

We are made right with God in the same way.

Through the same grace.

By the same faith.

In the same Jesus.

journeys.title: The Emmaus Road
journeys.subtitle: From troubled steps to joyful witness
journeys.description: Walk with the two disciples from confusion to joy as Jesus meets them on the road, opens the Scriptures, and reveals Himself. Each day will help you take a simple step with Jesus—hearing, trusting, and responding—until your heart is stirred to share the good news with others.

journeys.title: Walking With God
journeys.description: Description: Discover how a growing relationship with God becomes part of everyday life as you learn to listen, pray, trust, obey and keep walking with Him.

metadata.introductionContent:
You've come a long way.

You began by asking one of life's biggest questions:

Who is God?

Along the way, you've discovered that God created you in His Image and that your life has purpose and value.

You've seen what went wrong when humanity chose its own way instead of God's Way.

You've discovered why Jesus came, what He did for us at the Cross, and the New Life He offers.

But following Jesus isn't simply about what you've discovered.

It's about what happens next.

It's about Walking with God.

A Relationship with God isn't meant to exist only on Sundays or during moments that feel spiritual.

God wants to be part of your everyday life.

Your work.

Your relationships.

Your decisions.

Your joys.

Your disappointments.

Your questions.

Your future.

Walking with God means learning to listen to Him through Scripture.

Talking honestly with Him in Prayer.

Trusting Him when you don't understand.

Following His Ways when your way seems easier.

Recognising God's Presence in the ordinary moments of life.

And continuing to walk when you stumble.

You won't always get everything right.

You won't always feel close to God.

There will be seasons when your Faith feels strong and seasons when you have questions.

Keep walking.

Because the Christian Life isn't about reaching a point where you no longer need Jesus.

It's about learning, day after day, to walk with Him.

That's what we're going to explore in this final Walk of Come and See.

Not how to become a perfect Christian.

Simply how to keep walking with the God who has been inviting you closer from the very beginning.

Let's walk.

journeys.title: What Went Wrong?
journeys.description: Discover how sin entered God's good creation, what it has done to our relationship with God, ourselves and one another, and why humanity needs to be rescued.

metadata.introductionContent:
God created the world good.

He created humanity in His image.

He gave us purpose.

He created us for relationship—with Him and with one another.

But we don't have to look very far to realise that something has gone terribly wrong.

Our world is filled with pain.

Relationships break down.

People hurt one another.

We see hatred, greed, injustice, violence and suffering.

And if we're honest, the problem isn't only somewhere "out there."

We see it in ourselves too.

We do things we know we shouldn't do.

We hurt people we love.

We make choices we regret.

We know what is right and sometimes choose something else anyway.

So what happened?

The Bible takes us back to the beginning and shows us a moment when humanity chose to turn away from God's way and follow its own.

The Bible calls this **sin**.

Sin is more than breaking a list of religious rules.

At its heart, sin is choosing life **our way instead of God's way**.

And that choice has consequences.

Over the next few steps, we'll discover what sin is, how it damaged humanity's relationship with God, how its effects spread into every part of our world, and why none of us can simply fix the problem ourselves.

Some of what we discover may be uncomfortable.

But we need to understand what's wrong before we can understand why the good news of Jesus really is **good news**.

And thankfully, humanity's failure isn't where God's story ends.

journeys.title: Who is God?
journeys.description: Discover who God is, what He is like, how He has made Himself known, and why knowing Him changes everything.

metadata.completionMessage: You've taken your first step in discovering who God is. Keep walking—there is so much more to discover.
metadata.introductionContent:
Maybe you've believed in God for as long as you can remember.

Maybe you're not even sure that God exists.

Or perhaps you've been around church for years, but if someone asked you, "Who is God?" you'd struggle to know what to say.

Wherever you're starting from, you're welcome here.

The Bible doesn't begin by trying to prove God. It simply begins:

**"In the beginning God..."**

Those few words are the beginning of an extraordinary story—and they're the beginning of our journey too.

Over the next few steps, we're going to explore what the Bible reveals about God: who He is, what He is like, how He has made Himself known, and what any of this has to do with your life.

You don't need to understand everything before you begin.

You don't need to pretend you don't have questions.

Just come with an open heart.

Because the Christian faith isn't ultimately about knowing more *about* God.

It's about knowing **Him**.

Let's begin.

steps.title: Christ Is Not Divided
steps.mentor_intro:
The church in Corinth had many spiritual gifts.

It also had serious problems.

Paul begins by bringing the believers back to the foundation of their faith.

Jesus Christ and His Cross.
steps.teaching_content:
Corinth was a wealthy, influential and deeply immoral city.

Its position on a major trade route brought together people, ideas and religions from across the Roman world.

The culture valued wealth, status, impressive speech and personal success.

These values had entered the church.

The Corinthian believers began dividing themselves into groups centred around different leaders.

Some claimed to follow Paul.

Others preferred Apollos.

Others identified themselves with Peter.

They were comparing leaders, choosing favourites and treating the Church as though it were built around human personalities.

Paul asks a direct question.

Is Christ divided?

Paul had not been crucified for them.

They had not been baptized into the name of Apollos or Peter.

Only Jesus had gone to the Cross for them.

The Corinthians were impressed by human wisdom and powerful personalities.

But God’s wisdom is revealed most clearly through the Cross.

To the world, a crucified Messiah looked weak and foolish.

Yet through the Cross, God defeated sin and opened the way of salvation.

The Church is not built through human cleverness, popularity or reputation.

It is built upon Jesus Christ.

Paul had planted the church.

Apollos had helped it grow.

But God was the One who gave life.

Different leaders had different responsibilities, but they were servants working for the same Lord.

When Christians build their identity around a preacher, pastor, denomination or ministry, the Church becomes divided.

Leaders are gifts from God, but they are not the foundation.

Jesus is the foundation.

The Cross also removes our pride.

We did not save ourselves.

We cannot boast about our intelligence, background, gifting or spiritual experience.

Everything we have received has come through God’s grace.

The answer to division is not finding the perfect human leader.

It is returning to Jesus.

Have you ever allowed admiration for a Christian leader to become more important than your devotion to Jesus?

How does the Cross confront pride, competition and division within the Church?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for going to the Cross for me.

Forgive me for the times I have placed too much importance on human personalities, popularity or reputation.

You alone are the foundation of Your Church.

Remove pride and division from my heart.

Help me honour faithful leaders without placing them in the position that belongs only to You.

Keep my eyes fixed upon You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider whether loyalty to a leader, ministry or tradition has affected the way you see other believers.

Bring that attitude to the Cross and choose to honour Jesus above every human personality.

steps.title: Your Body Belongs to Jesus
steps.mentor_intro:
The Corinthians had separated spiritual life from physical life.

Paul reminds them that following Jesus includes what we do with our bodies.
steps.teaching_content:
Greek culture often treated the body and the spiritual life as separate.

Some people indulged every physical desire because they believed the body did not matter.

Others denied ordinary physical needs in an attempt to become more spiritual.

Still others idolized physical beauty and strength.

These ideas had influenced the Corinthian believers.

Some continued patterns of sexual immorality while claiming to belong to Jesus.

The church was even tolerating a sexual relationship that the surrounding culture considered shameful.

Paul refuses to treat this casually.

Grace does not make sin unimportant.

The Church must offer forgiveness to repentant sinners, but it must not approve behaviour that openly rejects the Lordship of Jesus.

Paul reminds the believers that their bodies belong to the Lord.

The body is not disposable or spiritually irrelevant.

It was created by God.

It was purchased through the death of Jesus.

It is joined to Christ.

It is a temple of the Holy Spirit.

What we do with our bodies affects our relationship with Jesus and with other people.

Sexual sin is never merely physical.

It joins together people whom God has not joined and damages what belongs to Him.

Paul therefore calls the believers to flee sexual immorality and honour God with their bodies.

This principle extends beyond sexuality.

The Corinthians were taking one another to court.

Some were becoming drunk during the Lord’s Supper.

Others were exercising their freedom without considering how their choices affected believers with more sensitive consciences.

They kept asking whether something was permitted.

Paul wanted them to ask a better question.

Will this honour Jesus?

Will it benefit others?

Will it build up the Church?

Christian freedom is not permission to be controlled by desire.

We belong to Jesus.

Because He purchased us at great cost, every part of life can now become an offering of worship to Him.

Are there areas of your physical life that you have tried to separate from your relationship with Jesus?

Do your choices merely satisfy what you want, or do they honour Jesus and build up others?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for purchasing me at such great cost.

My body belongs to You.

Forgive me for the ways I have treated physical choices as though they did not affect my spiritual life.

Cleanse me from sexual sin, harmful habits and selfish desires.

Fill me with the Holy Spirit.

Help me honour You through my body, relationships and choices.

May my freedom always be guided by love and obedience.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Bring one physical habit, desire or relationship honestly before Jesus.

Ask the Holy Spirit to show you whether it honours God and strengthens your witness.

steps.title: Gifts Governed by Love
steps.mentor_intro:
The Corinthian church had many spiritual gifts.

But spiritual gifts without God’s love were creating pride, competition and disorder.
steps.teaching_content:
The Holy Spirit gives different gifts to different believers.

One person may receive wisdom.

Another may receive knowledge, faith, healing, prophecy, discernment, tongues or interpretation.

The gifts are different, but they come from the same Holy Spirit.

They are not given to prove that one person is more spiritual than another.

They are given for the good of the whole Church.

Paul describes the Church as a body.

A body has many parts.

The eye cannot tell the hand that it is unnecessary.

The head cannot reject the feet.

Every member belongs.

Every gift matters.

And every part needs the others.

The Corinthians had begun comparing gifts and using them without considering their effect on other people.

Their gatherings became competitive and disorderly.

They were spiritually gifted, but they lacked the character needed to use those gifts well.

Paul responds by showing them the most excellent way.

Love.

Without love, the most impressive spiritual gift becomes empty noise.

Knowledge, faith, generosity and sacrifice lose their value when love is absent.

The love Paul describes is not merely an emotion.

It is the sacrificial love of God expressed through deliberate action.

Love is patient.

Love is kind.

Love does not envy or boast.

Love is not self-seeking.

It does not delight in evil.

It protects, trusts, hopes and perseveres.

Spiritual gifts are temporary.

Love will remain.

The Corinthians also needed correction concerning the Resurrection.

Some had begun questioning whether believers would be raised bodily from the dead.

Paul brings them back to the heart of the Gospel.

Jesus died for our sins.

He was buried.

He was raised.

He appeared to many witnesses.

The Resurrection is not an optional addition to Christianity.

If Jesus was not raised, our faith is empty.

But Jesus has been raised.

His Resurrection is the beginning and promise of the resurrection still to come.

The God who values our bodies now will one day raise and transform them.

Because Jesus lives, our service is never wasted.

We can use our gifts with humility, love and hope.

Are you more interested in being noticed for your gift or in using it to serve others?

Does the way you treat people reflect the love described in 1 Corinthians 13?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

Help me receive what You give without pride or comparison.

Teach me to honour every member of the Body of Christ.

Let Your love govern my words, choices and service.

Thank You that Jesus died, was buried and rose again.

Fill me with Resurrection hope.

Help me serve You faithfully, knowing that nothing done for Jesus is wasted.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Choose to use something God has given you to strengthen another person.

Serve quietly and lovingly without needing recognition.

steps.title: Strength Made Perfect in Weakness
steps.mentor_intro:
Second Corinthians allows us to see Paul’s heart more personally than any of his other letters.

He had been criticized, rejected and misunderstood.

Yet his confidence remained in God.
steps.teaching_content:
The relationship between Paul and the Corinthians had become painful.

False teachers questioned his authority and attacked his character.

They accused him of changing his plans, lacking courage and failing to speak impressively.

They judged ministry by outward appearance, reputation and strength.

Paul responds by showing them a very different picture of Christian leadership.

True ministry is not built around making ourselves look impressive.

We do not proclaim ourselves.

We proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord.

We are servants because of Jesus.

Paul describes believers as fragile jars of clay carrying a priceless treasure.

The weakness of the container makes it clear that the power comes from God.

Paul had experienced pressure, confusion, persecution and suffering.

Yet God had sustained him.

He could be hard pressed without being crushed.

Perplexed without surrendering to despair.

Persecuted without being abandoned.

Struck down without being destroyed.

His suffering was not proof that God had rejected him.

It became the place where the life and power of Jesus were revealed.

Paul also speaks about a painful weakness he repeatedly asked God to remove.

God did not remove it.

Instead, God assured Paul that His grace was sufficient and that His power was made perfect in weakness.

Paul learned to stop treating weakness as something that automatically disqualified him.

He could acknowledge his limitations because the power of Jesus rested upon him.

This does not mean that all weakness or suffering is good.

Nor does it mean we should avoid asking God for healing and deliverance.

It means our hope does not depend upon appearing strong.

God comforts us in our troubles so that we can comfort others.

He uses suffering to deepen our dependence upon Him.

He works through imperfect people who know that the treasure belongs to Him.

The world celebrates leaders who appear powerful, polished and self-sufficient.

Jesus forms servants who are humble, honest and dependent upon His grace.

Are you trying to hide a weakness because you believe it makes you useless to God?

How has God’s comfort during a difficult season equipped you to comfort someone else?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for being the God of all comfort.

Meet me in the places where I feel weak, pressured or misunderstood.

Forgive me for trying to appear stronger than I am.

Teach me to depend upon Your grace.

Let the life of Jesus be seen through my weakness.

Use what I have suffered to make me more compassionate towards others.

May it always be clear that the power belongs to You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Bring an area of weakness honestly before God.

Instead of only asking Him to remove it, also ask how His grace and power can be revealed through it.

steps.title: The Ministry of Reconciliation
steps.mentor_intro:
The love of Jesus changes what we live for.

Those who have been reconciled to God are called to carry His message of reconciliation to others.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul explains what motivates his ministry.

The love of Christ compels him.

Jesus died for all so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for the One who died and was raised for them.

Through Jesus, God was reconciling the world to Himself.

Our sin separated us from God.

At the Cross, Jesus carried our sin so that we might receive the righteousness of God.

God did not merely forgive us and leave us unchanged.

He made us new.

Anyone who is in Christ is a new creation.

The old has gone.

The new has come.

God now entrusts His people with the message of reconciliation.

We are Christ’s representatives.

Through our words and lives, God appeals to others to be reconciled to Him.

This calling requires discernment.

The Corinthians had become impressed by leaders who presented themselves as superior apostles.

They were polished, forceful and confident.

They criticized Paul while drawing attention to themselves.

Paul warns the church that outward appearance is not enough.

Falsehood can present itself as light.

A leader must be tested by faithfulness to the true Jesus, the true Holy Spirit and the true Gospel.

Paul’s concern was not merely to defend his reputation.

He feared that the Corinthians were being drawn away from sincere devotion to Jesus.

True Christian leadership does not exploit, control or enslave people.

It serves them and points them towards Jesus.

The Gospel also transforms the way we use money.

Paul encouraged the Corinthians to help believers suffering from famine.

He did not manipulate them into giving.

He pointed to the example of Jesus, who gave Himself for us.

Christian giving should be willing, generous and proportionate to what God has provided.

It is not a competition.

Those with more can help those with less so that needs are met within the family of God.

A reconciled life becomes a generous life.

We have received grace freely.

Now we carry grace to others.

We speak the Good News.

We protect the Church from false teaching.

We serve without exploiting people.

We give to those in need.

And through it all, we remain sincerely devoted to Jesus.

Does your life help people move towards reconciliation with God and with others?

Are you evaluating Christian leaders by their appearance and confidence, or by their faithfulness to Jesus and the Gospel?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for dying and rising for me.

Thank You for reconciling me to the Father and making me a new creation.

Let Your love shape what I live for.

Help me represent You faithfully.

Give me discernment to recognize teaching and leadership that draw people away from the true Gospel.

Protect my devotion to You.

Make me generous with what You have entrusted to me.

Use my words, service and giving to help others experience Your grace.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Ask Jesus how you can take part in His ministry of reconciliation.

Be willing to begin through a conversation, an apology, an act of generosity or an invitation back to God.

steps.title: 1 and 2 Corinthians: Walk Complete

content.text:
You have completed your Walk through 1 and 2 Corinthians.

You have seen that a church can possess spiritual gifts and still need deep transformation.

The Corinthians struggled with division, pride, immorality, disorder and false teaching.

Paul continued calling them back to Jesus.

Jesus alone was crucified for them.

Jesus alone is the foundation of the Church.

Their bodies belonged to Him.

Their spiritual gifts were given to serve others.

Their freedom had to be governed by love.

Their hope rested upon the Resurrection.

And their weakness became a place where the power of Jesus could be revealed.

These letters remind us that God does not give up easily on His people.

He corrects us because He loves us.

He calls us away from compromise and back to sincere devotion to Jesus.

You are part of the Body of Christ.

Your life matters.

Your body matters.

Your gifts matter.

Your love for others matters.

Continue building your life upon Jesus.

Use what the Holy Spirit has given you to strengthen others.

Remain faithful when you are misunderstood.

Trust God’s grace in your weakness.

And carry His message of reconciliation into the world.

Father,

steps.title: Faith, Love and Hope
steps.mentor_intro:
The believers in Thessalonica were young in their faith.

They faced immediate opposition.

Yet their transformed lives became an example to other churches.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul’s time in Thessalonica was brief.

He preached in the synagogue and explained from the Scriptures that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead.

Some Jewish people believed.

Many Gentiles also turned to Jesus.

But opposition soon became intense, and Paul had to leave the city.

The new believers were left behind in a hostile environment with very little opportunity to receive further teaching.

Paul was deeply concerned about them.

Would their new faith survive persecution?

When Timothy returned with news from Thessalonica, Paul was filled with gratitude.

The believers were not merely surviving.

They were growing.

Paul describes their Christian lives through three qualities.

Their work produced by faith.

Their labour prompted by love.

Their endurance inspired by hope in Jesus.

Faith was not merely something they claimed to believe.

It produced action.

Love was not simply a feeling.

It moved them to serve and sacrifice.

Hope was not wishful thinking.

It gave them strength to remain faithful under pressure.

The Gospel had come to them not only through words, but with power, the Holy Spirit and deep conviction.

Their lives changed so clearly that the news spread throughout the region.

People heard how they had turned from idols.

They had left their old loyalties behind.

They now served the living and true God.

And they were waiting for Jesus to return from Heaven.

These three movements describe Christian conversion.

We turn from what once controlled us.

We begin serving God.

We live in expectation of Jesus’ return.

The Thessalonians did not have years of Christian experience.

They did not have easy circumstances.

But the Gospel had taken root in them.

Their faith worked.

Their love laboured.

Their hope endured.

What has changed in your life because you have turned towards Jesus?

Are faith, love and hope producing visible fruit in the way you live?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for calling me away from everything that competes with You.

Strengthen my faith so that it produces obedience.

Fill me with love that is willing to serve.

Give me hope that endures when following Jesus becomes difficult.

Let the Gospel take deep root within me.

May the change in my life help others see that You are the living and true God.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider whether something from your old life is still competing with Jesus for your loyalty.

Turn from it and choose again to serve the living God.

steps.title: Sharing Our Lives
steps.mentor_intro:
Paul did not simply deliver a message to the Thessalonians.

He shared his life with them.

His ministry was marked by truth, tenderness and genuine love.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul had faced opposition before arriving in Thessalonica.

He and Silas had been beaten and imprisoned in Philippi.

Yet suffering did not silence them.

God gave them courage to proclaim the Gospel again.

Paul reminds the Thessalonians that his motives were not impure.

He was not trying to deceive them.

He did not use flattery.

He was not seeking money, status or human praise.

God had entrusted him with the Gospel, and he wanted to please God rather than people.

His ministry combined courage with tenderness.

Paul describes his care as being like that of a nursing mother.

He and his companions loved the believers so deeply that they shared not only the Gospel but their own lives.

He also describes his ministry as being like that of a father.

He encouraged, comforted and urged each believer to live in a way worthy of God.

Christian ministry is more than communicating correct information.

It includes opening our lives, caring for people and helping them grow.

The Thessalonians received Paul’s message as the Word of God.

That Word continued working within them.

But their faith brought opposition.

They suffered from people around them just as other churches had suffered.

Paul wanted to return and strengthen them, but he was repeatedly prevented from doing so.

He understood that spiritual opposition was trying to separate him from the young church.

Unable to go himself, Paul sent Timothy.

Timothy returned with encouraging news about their faith and love.

They still remembered Paul warmly.

They were standing firm in the Lord.

Their faith brought new strength to Paul during his own distress.

This is genuine fellowship.

Paul strengthened them.

Their faith then strengthened him.

In the Body of Christ, encouragement flows in both directions.

Even mature leaders need the prayers, faith and encouragement of other believers.

Do you share only Christian information with people, or are you willing to share your life with them?

Who has strengthened your faith through sincere care, encouragement and example?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Purify my motives as I serve others.

Keep me from seeking praise, control or personal advantage.

Give me courage to speak the truth and tenderness to care for people well.

Teach me to share both the Gospel and my life.

Make me willing to encourage others and humble enough to receive encouragement from them.

Strengthen Your Church through genuine fellowship.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Encourage someone whose faith has strengthened you.

Tell them specifically how God has used their life to help you continue following Jesus.

steps.title: A Life That Pleases God
steps.mentor_intro:
Coming to Jesus is the beginning of a journey.

Paul urges the Thessalonians to continue growing in holiness and living in a way that pleases God.
steps.teaching_content:
The Thessalonians had already begun living for Jesus.

Paul does not tell them to become comfortable with their present progress.

He urges them to grow more and more.

God’s will for His people includes holiness.

The culture around Thessalonica treated sexual immorality casually.

Paul calls believers to live differently.

They must learn to control their bodies in a way that is holy and honourable.

Other people must never be treated as objects for satisfying desire.

Sexual choices are part of our discipleship.

God has not called us to impurity.

He has called us to a holy life.

Rejecting this instruction is not merely rejecting human advice.

It is resisting the God who gives us the Holy Spirit.

Holiness also affects the way we love.

The Thessalonians were already showing love towards other believers.

Paul encourages them to keep growing in it.

Christian maturity never reaches the point where love is no longer needed.

Paul also addresses ordinary work.

Believers should live responsibly, attend to their work and avoid becoming unnecessarily dependent upon others.

Faithfulness in ordinary responsibilities is part of our witness.

God is interested not only in the work we do but in the character with which we do it.

Paul closes his first letter with practical instructions for life together.

Respect those who care for and lead the church.

Live at peace with one another.

Warn those who are irresponsible.

Encourage the discouraged.

Help the weak.

Be patient with everyone.

Do not repay wrong with wrong.

Pursue what is good.

Rejoice.

Pray continually.

Give thanks in every circumstance.

Remain open to the work of the Holy Spirit while testing everything carefully.

Hold firmly to what is good.

Reject every form of evil.

Holiness is not produced by human strength alone.

Paul prays that the God of peace will sanctify them completely.

God calls us to holiness.

And the God who calls us is faithful to continue His work within us.

Is there an area of your life that you have excluded from God’s call to holiness?

What would it mean to live faithfully for Jesus through your ordinary work and responsibilities?
steps.prayer:
God of peace,

Continue Your work of holiness within me.

Purify my thoughts, desires, relationships and choices.

Help me honour You with my body.

Teach me to love more deeply, work faithfully and live responsibly.

Give me patience with others and compassion for those who are weak or discouraged.

Keep me prayerful, thankful and responsive to the Holy Spirit.

You are faithful.

Complete what You have begun in me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Bring an area of compromise honestly before God.

Ask the Holy Spirit to help you respond with obedience and begin living in a way that honours Jesus.

steps.title: Hope When Jesus Returns
steps.mentor_intro:
Some believers in Thessalonica had died.

The church feared that those who had died might miss the return of Jesus.

Paul writes to replace their confusion with hope.
steps.teaching_content:
Christians grieve when someone dies.

But we do not grieve as people who have no hope.

Our hope is rooted in what God has already done.

Jesus died.

Jesus rose again.

Because Jesus lives, those who belong to Him will also be raised.

When Jesus returns, believers who have died will not be forgotten or disadvantaged.

They will be raised.

Those who are still alive will be gathered together with them to meet the Lord.

God’s people will be united.

And we will be with Jesus forever.

Paul gives this teaching so that believers can encourage one another.

The return of Jesus is not meant to produce empty speculation.

It is meant to bring comfort, courage and holy living.

Paul then explains that the Day of the Lord will come unexpectedly upon a world that is unprepared.

Believers should not live in darkness or spiritual sleep.

We belong to the light.

We are called to remain awake, clear-minded and ready.

Faith and love protect our hearts.

The hope of salvation protects our minds.

God has not called His people to suffer His wrath but to receive salvation through Jesus Christ.

Jesus died so that we may live together with Him.

The timing of His return has often caused distraction and argument.

Paul’s emphasis is not upon calculating dates.

It is upon readiness.

Those waiting for Jesus should encourage one another and help each other grow.

Biblical hope is not an escape from present responsibilities.

It gives us a reason to live faithfully now.

Death does not have the final word.

Suffering does not have the final word.

Jesus will return.

The dead will be raised.

God’s people will be gathered.

And we will be with the Lord forever.

How does the Resurrection of Jesus change the way you face death and grief?

If you truly expected Jesus to return, what would change about the way you live now?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You that You died and rose again.

Thank You that death does not have the final word.

Comfort me where I carry grief.

Fill me with the hope of Resurrection.

Help me remain spiritually awake and ready for Your return.

Let faith, love and hope shape the way I live.

Use me to encourage others with the promise that we will be with You forever.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Bring someone you are grieving before Jesus.

Thank Him that everyone who belongs to Him remains secure in the hope of Resurrection.

steps.title: Stand Firm and Keep Working
steps.mentor_intro:
The Thessalonians remained under intense pressure.

They also received confusing claims that the Day of the Lord had already arrived.

Paul calls them to stand firm, remain calm and continue living faithfully.
steps.teaching_content:
The Thessalonians’ faith and love continued growing despite persecution.

Paul assures them that God sees their suffering.

In the present, injustice may appear to succeed.

But God’s final judgement will be completely just.

Jesus will return.

Those who oppose God will answer to Him.

Those who belong to Jesus will share in His glory.

This truth should produce perseverance rather than revenge.

Judgement belongs to God.

The believers had also become confused about the return of Jesus.

Some had been told that the Day of the Lord had already come.

The claim may even have arrived through a message or letter falsely attributed to Paul.

Paul tells them not to become unsettled or alarmed.

Certain events still had to occur before Jesus returned.

A great rebellion would come.

A lawless ruler would oppose God, exalt himself and deceive many.

Yet evil would not have the final word.

Jesus would overthrow the lawless one through the splendour of His coming.

The influence of lawlessness was already at work, but it remained under God’s restraint.

Believers did not need to panic.

They needed to stand firm and hold to the truth they had received.

Some had responded to teaching about the Second Coming by giving up their work.

They believed there was no reason to continue with ordinary responsibilities if Jesus was returning soon.

Paul corrects them firmly.

Waiting for Jesus is not an excuse for laziness or irresponsibility.

Those who are able to work should do so faithfully.

Paul is not condemning people who cannot find work or are unable to work.

He addresses those who refuse to work and become disruptive or dependent upon others by choice.

The return of Jesus should make us more faithful, not less.

When Jesus comes, He should find us doing what He has entrusted to us.

Paul ends with encouragement.

Do not become tired of doing what is good.

Keep walking in holiness.

Keep waiting with hope.

Keep working faithfully.

Keep praying for the Gospel to spread.

The Christian life involves both walking and waiting.

We walk faithfully with Jesus in the present.

We wait expectantly for Him to return.

Does thinking about the return of Jesus make you more faithful in your present responsibilities?

Are fear and speculation distracting you from standing firmly in the truth?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You that You will return and bring perfect justice.

Strengthen believers who are suffering for their faith.

Protect me from fear, deception and unhealthy speculation.

Help me stand firmly in the truth.

Teach me to wait for You while remaining faithful in the work You have given me.

Keep me from becoming tired of doing good.

May my life be marked by holiness, hope and faithful service until You come.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Approach your present responsibilities as work entrusted to you by Jesus.

Ask Him to help you remain faithful while you wait for His return.

steps.title: 1 and 2 Thessalonians: Walk Complete

content.text: llll

You have completed the 1 and 2 Thessalonians Walk.

You have seen how faith works, love serves and hope endures.

The Thessalonian believers turned from idols to serve the living God and to wait for His Son from Heaven. Although they faced persecution and uncertainty, they continued growing in faith and love.

You have been encouraged to walk in holiness, care for others, work faithfully and remain responsive to the Holy Spirit.

You have also discovered that followers of Jesus do not grieve without hope. Jesus died and rose again, and those who belong to Him will be raised when He returns.

The promise of His return should not produce fear, speculation or inactivity. It should strengthen us to stand firm, live responsibly and never grow tired of doing good.

Keep walking faithfully.

Keep waiting expectantly.

Jesus will return.

Lord Jesus, thank You for strengthening my faith, deepening my love and renewing my hope.

Teach me to live in a way that pleases You. Make me holy in my thoughts, relationships and actions.

Comfort me when I grieve and remind me that death does not have the final word. You died and rose again, and all who belong to You will share in Your victory.

Protect me from fear, confusion and deception. Help me remain grounded in Your truth and responsive to the Holy Spirit.

Give me strength to serve faithfully, work responsibly and never grow tired of doing good.

Keep me alert, steadfast and hopeful as I wait for Your return.

May my life honour You until the day I see You face to face.

Amen.

steps.prayer:
Lord Jesus, thank You for strengthening my faith, deepening my love and renewing my hope.

Teach me to live in a way that pleases You. Make me holy in my thoughts, relationships and actions.

Comfort me when I grieve and remind me that death does not have the final word. You died and rose again, and all who belong to You will share in Your victory.

Protect me from fear, confusion and deception. Help me remain grounded in Your truth and responsive to the Holy Spirit.

Give me strength to serve faithfully, work responsibly and never grow tired of doing good.

Keep me alert, steadfast and hopeful as I wait for Your return.

May my life honour You until the day I see You face to face.

Amen.

steps.title: Guard the Truth
steps.mentor_intro:
Welcome to the combined Walk through 1 and 2 Timothy.

Timothy was a younger leader serving the church in Ephesus. He faced false teaching, difficult people and the heavy responsibility of caring for God’s people.

Paul begins by reminding Timothy why he was left in Ephesus: he must protect the church from teaching that distracts people from the truth.
steps.teaching_content:
False teaching was creating speculation and controversy rather than helping people grow in faith.

The goal of sound teaching is not to win arguments or display knowledge. It is love that comes from a pure heart, a good conscience and sincere faith.

Paul never forgot the mercy Jesus had shown him. He had once opposed Christ and persecuted His people, yet Jesus saved him and entrusted him with ministry.

Grace did not cause Paul to treat sin lightly. It filled him with gratitude and gave him a new purpose.

Timothy must hold firmly to both faith and a good conscience. Truth must be believed, taught and lived.

The church does not guard the Gospel by becoming harsh or argumentative. We protect the truth by remaining faithful to Jesus, rejecting distortion and allowing God’s grace to shape our character.

Are there voices or ideas influencing you more deeply than the teaching of Jesus?

Does your knowledge of Scripture lead you towards love, a good conscience and sincere faith?

How does remembering God’s mercy help you remain humble?
steps.prayer:
Lord Jesus, thank You for the mercy and grace You have shown me.

Help me remain faithful to the Gospel and recognise teaching that leads people away from You.

Give me a pure heart, a good conscience and sincere faith.

May the truth I believe produce love in the way I live.

Amen.
steps.todays_action: Return to the truth of the Gospel. Allow gratitude for God’s mercy to shape your words, choices and relationships.

steps.title: God’s Household
steps.mentor_intro:
The church is more than an organisation or a weekly gathering.

It is God’s Household, the church of the living God and a pillar and foundation of the truth.

Today we consider how prayer, character and godly leadership help the church reflect Jesus.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul calls the church to pray for all people, including those in authority. God desires people to be saved and to come to a knowledge of the truth.

There is one God and one Mediator between God and humanity: Christ Jesus, who gave Himself as a ransom for all people.

Prayer and mission belong together. As the church prays for the world, it remembers that the Gospel is for everyone.

Paul then describes the character required of those who lead and serve. His emphasis is not on popularity, talent or status. Christian leadership must be supported by a life of integrity.

Leaders should be faithful, self-controlled, hospitable, gentle, spiritually mature and respected. Their conduct at home and among others matters because leadership in God’s Household is an expression of character.

At the centre of the church is Jesus Christ. He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, proclaimed among the nations, believed on in the world and taken up in glory.

The church belongs to Him, represents Him and must be shaped by His truth.

What place does prayer for other people have in your life?

Why does Christian character matter as much as ability in leadership?

How can your conduct help others see the truth and goodness of Jesus?
steps.prayer:
Father, thank You that Your desire is for people to be saved and know the truth.

Teach me to pray for others and to live with Your mission in view.

Develop integrity, gentleness, faithfulness and self-control within me.

Help Your Church reflect the character of Jesus and remain grounded in His truth.

Amen.
steps.todays_action: Pray for your church, its leaders and those who do not yet know Jesus. Let your conduct support the faith you profess.

steps.title: Train Yourself in Godliness
steps.mentor_intro:
Following Jesus requires more than recognising false teaching.

We must also grow in truth, godliness and contentment.

Paul encourages Timothy not to be intimidated by his youth, but to become an example through the way he lives.
steps.teaching_content:
Some people in Ephesus were presenting human restrictions as spiritual maturity. Paul teaches that everything God created is good when it is received with thanksgiving and guided by God’s Word and prayer.

Timothy must nourish himself with the truths of the faith and train himself in godliness.

This training involves his whole life. He is to set an example in speech, conduct, love, faith and purity. He must devote himself to Scripture, teaching and the gift God has given him.

Spiritual influence does not depend primarily upon age. A life that consistently reflects Jesus can strengthen others and protect the church.

Paul also warns about the love of money. Money itself is not condemned, but the desire to become rich can draw people away from faith and produce deep sorrow.

Godliness with contentment is great gain. We entered the world with nothing and will take nothing from it.

Those with resources should not place their hope in wealth. They should hope in God, enjoy His provision with gratitude and become rich in good deeds, generosity and willingness to share.

What is shaping your spiritual growth and character?

Would others see an example of Jesus in your speech, conduct, love, faith and purity?

Is your security found in God or in what you possess?
steps.prayer:
Lord, train my heart in godliness.

Help me receive Your gifts with gratitude without allowing them to take Your place.

Make my speech, conduct, love, faith and purity an example that points others towards Jesus.

Protect me from greed and teach me the freedom of contentment and generosity.

Amen.
steps.todays_action: Pay attention to the example your life is setting. Receive God’s provision gratefully and hold what you possess with open hands.

steps.title: Guard the Good Deposit
steps.mentor_intro:
Second Timothy carries the weight of a final message.

Paul is imprisoned, suffering for the Gospel and approaching the end of his life. Timothy may feel fearful and discouraged.

Paul calls him to courage, endurance and faithfulness.
steps.teaching_content:
Timothy’s sincere faith had lived first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. He had received a spiritual heritage, but he now had to live faithfully for himself.

Paul tells Timothy to fan into flame the gift of God. The Holy Spirit does not produce cowardice, but power, love and self-discipline.

Timothy must not be ashamed of Jesus or of Paul’s suffering. The Gospel is worth suffering for because Jesus has destroyed death and brought life and immortality to light.

Paul is suffering, but he is not ashamed. His confidence rests in the One he has believed.

Timothy must guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit and entrust the truth to faithful people who will teach others.

Paul uses the pictures of a soldier, an athlete and a hardworking farmer. Each communicates focused devotion, discipline and patient endurance.

A faithful servant handles the Word of truth correctly. He does not reshape Scripture to suit himself or become distracted by fruitless arguments.

The Gospel must be preserved, lived and passed on.

Has fear caused you to hold back from serving or speaking about Jesus?

What spiritual gift or responsibility needs to be stirred into fresh life?

Are you receiving God’s truth in a way that enables you to pass it faithfully to others?
steps.prayer:
Holy Spirit, replace my fear with Your power, love and self-discipline.

Help me remain unashamed of Jesus and faithful to the Gospel.

Give me endurance when following You becomes difficult.

Teach me to handle Your Word correctly and pass its truth faithfully to others.

Guard what You have entrusted to me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action: Do not allow fear or discouragement to silence your faith. Keep serving with the strength that comes through the grace of Christ Jesus.

steps.title: Finish the Race
steps.mentor_intro:
Paul ends his final letter with an urgent charge.

Difficult times will come. People will resist the truth, and Timothy will face pressure to tell people what they want to hear.

Yet he must continue in Scripture, preach the Word and complete the work God has given him.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul describes people who appear religious but deny the transforming power of God. Their lives are shaped by pride, greed, pleasure and self-interest rather than love for God.

Timothy must be different.

He has observed Paul’s teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, endurance and suffering. He knows that faithfulness to Jesus can be costly.

His stability will come from continuing in the Holy Scriptures. Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, correcting and training in righteousness. Through it, God equips His people for every good work.

Timothy must proclaim the Word with patience and careful instruction. He must remain steady when people reject sound teaching and search for messages that satisfy their own desires.

Paul can now look back over his life and say that he has fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith.

He has experienced loneliness and opposition, but the Lord stood beside him and gave him strength.

Finishing well does not mean life has been easy. It means remaining faithful to Jesus through every season, trusting that He will bring His people safely into His Heavenly Kingdom.

Are you allowing Scripture to teach, correct and train you?

What might tempt you to compromise the truth or tell people only what they want to hear?

If you continue on your present path, are you becoming someone who will finish the race faithfully?
steps.prayer:
Lord Jesus, help me continue in Your truth.

Use Scripture to teach, correct, train and equip me for every good work.

Give me courage to remain faithful when Your truth is unpopular.

Stand beside me when I feel alone and strengthen me when the journey becomes difficult.

May I fight the good fight, finish the race and keep the faith.

To You be glory forever and ever.

Amen.
steps.todays_action: Continue faithfully in Scripture and in the work God has entrusted to you. Trust the Lord to stand with you and give you strength until the race is complete.

steps.title: 1 and 2 Timothy: Walk Complete

content.text: lll

You have completed the 1 and 2 Timothy Walk.

You have seen how Paul encouraged Timothy to guard the truth, develop godly character and remain faithful in difficult times.

The church is God’s Household. It must be grounded in Scripture, devoted to prayer and led by people whose character reflects Jesus.

The Gospel is not something we merely understand. It must shape our speech, conduct, love, faith and purity.

You have also been reminded that the Holy Spirit does not produce fear. He gives power, love and self-discipline.

There may be opposition, disappointment and loneliness, but the Lord remains faithful. He stands beside His people and gives them strength.

Continue in Scripture.

Guard what God has entrusted to you.

Live the Gospel with courage and integrity.

Pass the truth faithfully to others.

Keep fighting the good fight.

Keep running the race.

Keep the faith.

Lord Jesus, thank You for everything You have taught me through 1 and 2 Timothy.

Help me guard the truth without becoming proud, harsh or argumentative.

May sound teaching produce love, sincere faith and a good conscience within me.

Develop godly character in my speech, conduct, relationships and choices.

Holy Spirit, replace fear with Your power, love and self-discipline.

Help me remain unashamed of Jesus and faithful to the Gospel when following You becomes difficult.

Teach me to handle Scripture correctly and pass its truth faithfully to others.

Protect me from greed and lead me into contentment, gratitude and generosity.

Stand beside me when I feel alone and strengthen me when I become discouraged.

May I fight the good fight, finish the race and keep the faith.

To You be glory forever and ever.

Amen.
