steps.title: Come and See

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll continue walking together.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

You don't need to know everything today.

You simply need to take one more step with Jesus.
steps.teaching_content:
Two ordinary men heard John the Baptist speak about Jesus.

Curious, they began to follow Him.

Jesus turned and asked them,

"What are you seeking?"

It wasn't because He didn't know.

It was because they needed to know.

That question still matters today.

Why are you here?

Are you looking for hope?

Peace?

Forgiveness?

A fresh start?

Or are you simply curious about Jesus?

Whatever brought you here...

Jesus welcomes honest seekers.

He doesn't ask you to have all the answers before you come to Him.

He simply invites you to begin walking with Him.

Today isn't about completing a lesson.

It's about taking your first step towards knowing Jesus.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You for welcoming people who are still searching.

Thank You for inviting me to come to You just as I am.

Help me to know You a little better today and to keep taking one step at a time.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
If you have a few quiet moments today, read the rest of John chapter 1.

As you read, ask yourself one simple question:

What does this teach me about Jesus?

Don't worry if you don't understand everything.

Just keep looking at Him.

steps.title: Jesus Knows Your Name

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll continue walking together.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

I'm glad you're back.

Yesterday, Jesus invited you to come and see.

Today, you'll discover something even more personal.

He already knows you.
steps.teaching_content:
Andrew had only just met Jesus.

Before long, he brought his brother Simon to meet Him too.

Jesus looked at Simon and immediately called him by name.

Then He gave him a new name.

Peter.

Jesus wasn't simply identifying him.

He was revealing who Simon could become.

That's still how Jesus works today.

He knows your past.

He knows your struggles.

He knows your fears.

He also knows the person He is shaping you to become.

You may only see your weaknesses.

Jesus sees your future.

He doesn't wait until you've changed before calling you.

He calls you first...

and then begins changing you.

Take a quiet moment to thank Him for knowing you completely—and loving you anyway.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You that You know me completely.

Nothing about my life is hidden from You.

Thank You for loving me as I am, while patiently shaping me into the person You created me to be.

Help me trust the work You are doing in my life, even when I cannot yet see it.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
If you have a few quiet moments today,

as you go through John 1, look for what Jesus sees in the people He calls.

Then ask yourself:

What might Jesus be shaping in me?

Don't worry if you don't have all the answers.

Keep walking with Him.

steps.title: Follow Me

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll continue walking together.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

I'm grateful you're walking with Jesus again today.

Over the last two days you've discovered that Jesus welcomes you and knows you personally.

Today, He extends an invitation.

Not just to believe something about Him...

but to follow Him.
steps.teaching_content:
When Jesus found Philip, He didn't give him a long explanation.

He simply said,

"Follow Me."

Those two words changed Philip's life forever.

Following Jesus isn't about having every question answered before taking the first step.

It's about trusting the One who is leading you.

Philip didn't keep the invitation to himself.

He immediately found Nathanael and shared the good news with him.

Nathanael wasn't convinced.

He had questions.

He even doubted whether anything good could come from Nazareth.

Philip didn't argue.

He simply said,

"Come and see."

That's often the best response we can give.

We don't have to know everything.

We don't have to win every debate.

We simply keep following Jesus and invite others to discover Him for themselves.

Jesus is patient with honest questions.

He welcomes people who are willing to come and see.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You for inviting me to follow You.

Help me trust You even when I don't have every answer.

Teach me to take the next step in faith and to gently point others towards You.

May my life make people curious about Jesus.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
As you go through today, ask yourself one simple question:

"What would following Jesus look like in this situation?"

Whether you're at home, at work, at school or with friends, let that question guide one decision today.

Remember...

Following Jesus happens one step at a time.

steps.title: Jesus Sees You

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll continue walking together.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

I'm thankful you've come back today.

Sometimes we wonder if anyone really understands us.

Today, we'll meet a man who discovered that Jesus saw him long before they ever met.
steps.teaching_content:
When Nathanael approached Jesus, he expected to meet a stranger.

Instead, Jesus spoke as someone who already knew him.

Before Nathanael had taken a single step towards Jesus, Jesus had already seen him sitting under the fig tree.

We aren't told why Nathanael was there.

Perhaps he was praying.

Perhaps he was reading Scripture.

Perhaps he was simply alone with his thoughts.

Whatever happened beneath that tree, it mattered enough that Jesus mentioned it.

That changed everything.

The same Jesus sees you today.

He sees the parts of your life that nobody else notices.

He sees your joys.

He sees your disappointments.

He sees your prayers that nobody has heard.

He sees your quiet acts of faithfulness.

Nothing about your life escapes His attention.

You never have to fight for His attention.

You already have it.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You that nothing in my life is hidden from You.

Thank You for seeing me completely and loving me faithfully.

Help me remember that even when I feel unnoticed by others, I am always known and seen by You.

Teach me to trust Your presence every day.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few quiet moments today and remember one time when God faithfully cared for you.

Thank Him for it.

Then ask Him to help you notice His presence again today, even in ordinary moments.

He is nearer than you think.

steps.title: Jesus Brings New Life

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll continue walking together.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

It's good to be walking with you again today.

Over the last few days, we've been discovering who Jesus is.

Today, we'll see what happens when He steps into an ordinary situation.
steps.teaching_content:
A wedding should have been filled with celebration.

Instead, the hosts faced embarrassment.

The wine had run out.

For the families involved, this wasn't a small inconvenience. It was a moment of disappointment and shame.

Nobody expected Jesus to solve the problem.

Yet He quietly stepped into the situation and changed everything.

The ordinary jars of water became the finest wine.

That's the first miracle John records, and it's no accident.

From the very beginning, Jesus shows us that He brings new life where people have run out.

Perhaps today you've run out too.

Maybe you've run out of hope.

Or strength.

Or peace.

Or joy.

Jesus still specialises in bringing new life to places that seem empty.

He doesn't always work the way we expect.

But He is always able to do far more than we can imagine.

Nothing is beyond His power.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You that You bring new life into places that feel empty.

Where I have run out of hope, fill me with Your peace.

Where I feel weak, strengthen me.

Help me trust that nothing is impossible for You.

Teach me to bring every part of my life to You, knowing that You are able to transform it.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few moments today to think about one area of your life where you need Jesus to work.

Tell Him honestly.

You don't need impressive words.

Simply place that situation into His hands and trust Him with it.

He is still the God who brings new life.

steps.title: Jesus Changes What Matters

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll begin a new stage of our journey together as we discover why Jesus came.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

It's good to spend this time with Jesus again.

Over the last few days you've discovered who Jesus is.

Today we'll discover something else.

Where Jesus is welcomed, lives begin to change.
steps.teaching_content:
When Jesus entered the temple, He didn't see what everyone else saw.

People saw a busy place of worship.

Jesus saw a place that had lost its purpose.

The temple had become filled with noise, business and distraction, while the worship of God had been pushed into the background.

Jesus wasn't angry because people were buying and selling.

He was passionate because His Father's House had become something it was never meant to be.

As we follow Jesus, He gently begins doing the same work in our lives.

He lovingly shows us attitudes that need changing.

Habits that hold us back.

Priorities that have quietly taken God's place.

This isn't about making us feel guilty.

It's about making room for something better.

Jesus never removes something good without offering something greater.

The closer we walk with Him, the more our lives begin to reflect what matters most.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You for loving me enough to change me.

Help me recognise the areas of my life where You want to do Your work.

Give me the humility to trust You, even when change feels uncomfortable.

Teach me to love what You love and to place You at the very centre of my life.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few quiet moments today and ask yourself:

"Is there anything that's becoming more important to me than Jesus?"

Don't be afraid of the answer.

Simply place that area before Him and ask Him to shape your heart.

Real change begins when we trust Him.

steps.title: Born Again

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll continue walking together.

steps.mentor_intro: Good morning. It's good to spend this time with Jesus again. Today we're going to discover why following Jesus is more than becoming a better person—it is receiving a brand new life.
steps.teaching_content:
Nicodemus was a respected religious leader. He knew the Scriptures, lived a moral life and sincerely wanted to understand Jesus. Yet Jesus told him something surprising: "You must be born again."

Jesus wasn't saying that we simply need to try harder or become more religious. He was teaching that real life with God begins when He changes us from the inside out. It's a work of God's Spirit, not something we can achieve by our own efforts.

Many people spend years trying to improve themselves, hoping they'll eventually be good enough for God. But the Gospel is not about earning God's acceptance. It's about receiving the new life that Jesus freely offers through faith in Him.

When you trust Jesus, He doesn't just forgive your past—He begins transforming your heart, your desires and the direction of your life. Growth takes time, but the journey begins with new life that only He can give.

If you've already placed your trust in Jesus, thank Him for making you new. If you're still exploring who Jesus is, know that His invitation is open to you today.
steps.prayer: Father, thank You for the new life You offer through Jesus Christ. I know I cannot save myself or change my own heart. Please continue Your work in me, making me more like Jesus each day. Help me to trust You and follow wherever You lead. Amen.
steps.todays_action: Spend a few minutes thanking God for one way He has already changed your life. If you're still seeking Him, simply pray, "Jesus, help me to know You and understand what it means to be born again."

steps.title: God Loves You

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover where true satisfaction is found.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Yesterday, Jesus spoke about being born again.

Today, you'll discover why He came.
steps.teaching_content:
Perhaps the most famous verse in the Bible begins with two simple words.

"For God..."

Before we loved God...

He loved us.

Before we searched for Him...

He was searching for us.

Jesus tells us that God loved the world so much that He gave His only Son.

That's the heart of the gospel.

God didn't send Jesus because people deserved Him.

He sent Jesus because He loves them.

That includes you.

Jesus didn't come to condemn you.

He came to rescue you.

To forgive you.

To bring you into a relationship with the Father.

Love is where your journey with Jesus begins.

And it's where it continues every day.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for loving me long before I ever thought about You.

Thank You for sending Jesus so that I could know You.

Help me to live each day knowing that I am loved by You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few quiet moments today.

Read John 3:16 again.

This time, read it slowly.

Thank God that His love includes you.

steps.title: Living Water

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover the kind of faith that trusts Jesus at His word.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today you'll meet someone whose life was changed by one encounter with Jesus.
steps.teaching_content:
The woman came to the well expecting an ordinary day.

Instead, she met Jesus.

Most people avoided her.

Jesus didn't.

He knew everything about her.

Her disappointments.

Her mistakes.

Her brokenness.

Yet He stayed.

Then Jesus offered her something she had never imagined.

Living water.

Not water that satisfies for a little while...

Life that satisfies forever.

Like that woman, we often try to satisfy the deepest needs of our hearts with things that were never meant to.

Success.

Money.

Relationships.

Achievement.

For a moment they seem enough.

Then the thirst returns.

Jesus offers something different.

He offers Himself.

You don't have to earn His love.

You don't have to hide your past.

You don't have to pretend to be someone you're not.

Come to Him honestly.

He already knows your story.

And He still invites you to walk with Him.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You that Jesus knows me completely and still welcomes me.

Help me to find my hope and satisfaction in Him alone.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Spend a few quiet moments with Jesus today.

Ask Him to show you where you've been looking for satisfaction apart from Him.

Trust Him to fill your heart with the life only He can give.

steps.title: Faith That Trusts Jesus

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover what happens when Jesus meets someone who has lost hope.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today we'll meet a man who believed Jesus before he saw the answer.
steps.teaching_content:
An official came to Jesus because his son was dying.

He was desperate.

He begged Jesus to come with him.

Instead, Jesus simply said,

"Go. Your son will live."

The man had a choice.

He could insist that Jesus come with him.

Or he could trust Jesus' word.

He chose to believe.

Before he saw any evidence...

Before he received any confirmation...

He trusted Jesus.

That is what faith looks like.

Sometimes we want God to show us everything before we obey Him.

But Jesus often invites us to trust Him first.

His Word is trustworthy.

His promises are sure.

Even when we cannot yet see what He is doing.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Help me to trust Your Word, even when I cannot yet see the outcome.

Strengthen my faith and teach me to walk confidently with Jesus.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Think of one area where you need to trust God today.

Choose to believe His promises before you see the answer.

steps.title: Do You Want to Get Well?

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover the incredible life that Jesus offers to everyone who believes in Him.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today we'll meet a man who had almost given up hope.
steps.teaching_content:
For thirty-eight years, this man had lived with his condition.

Every day looked the same.

Every day he waited for something to change.

Then Jesus came to him.

Jesus asked a surprising question.

"Do you want to get well?"

The man began explaining why nothing had changed.

There was no one to help him.

Someone always got there first.

He had learned to expect disappointment.

Jesus didn't argue with his excuses.

He simply said,

"Get up. Pick up your mat and walk."

Immediately, everything changed.

Sometimes we become so used to our struggles that we stop believing anything can be different.

But Jesus is not limited by how long you've carried your burden.

He sees what others overlook.

He knows what you've been through.

And He still has the power to bring hope where it has been lost.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You that nothing is beyond Your power.

Help me to trust Jesus, even in the places where I have lost hope.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Bring one area of your life to Jesus today where you've stopped expecting change.

Ask Him to renew your hope.

steps.title: Jesus Gives Life

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll learn why knowing the truth about Jesus is more important than simply knowing about Him.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today Jesus speaks about the greatest gift He has come to give.
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus didn't come simply to improve our lives.

He came to give us life.

Real life.

Life with God that begins today and lasts forever.

Jesus said that everyone who hears His word and believes in the Father has eternal life.

That is wonderful news.

Because none of us could ever earn God's acceptance.

We all fall short.

Yet Jesus offers life as a gift.

Not because we deserve it.

But because He loves us.

Following Jesus is not about trying harder to impress God.

It is about trusting the One who has already done everything necessary to bring us back to Him.

The more you know Jesus, the more you discover that life is found in Him alone.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for giving me life through Jesus.

Help me to trust Him more each day and to live with the confidence that I belong to You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few moments today to thank Jesus for the new life He freely offers.

Rest in His grace instead of trying to earn His love.

steps.title: The Witnesses to Jesus

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover how Jesus satisfies the deepest hunger of the human heart.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today Jesus reminds us that God has given us every reason to believe in Him.
steps.teaching_content:
Many people asked Jesus why they should believe His words.

Jesus pointed to the evidence.

John the Baptist spoke about Him.

His miracles revealed God's power.

The Scriptures pointed to Him.

Everything was directing people towards Jesus.

Yet many still refused to believe.

The problem wasn't a lack of evidence.

It was an unwillingness to come to Him.

The same choice remains today.

We can know facts about Jesus without truly knowing Him.

Or we can come to Him with open hearts and discover the life He offers.

Christianity is not simply about learning information.

It is about knowing a Person.

As you continue this journey, don't just collect knowledge.

Allow every page of Scripture to lead you closer to Jesus Himself.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for revealing Jesus so clearly.

Open my heart to know Him more deeply and to trust Him with my whole life.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Read today's passage again later if you can.

Ask God to help you see Jesus more clearly through His Word.

steps.title: The Bread of Life

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover what it means to trust Jesus completely.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today we'll discover that Jesus offers something far greater than temporary satisfaction.
steps.teaching_content:
After Jesus fed the crowd, many people followed Him because they wanted more bread.

They had seen a miracle.

They wanted another one.

Jesus gently pointed them to something much greater.

He said,

"I am the bread of life."

Bread satisfies our hunger for a while.

Then we become hungry again.

The same is true of many things we chase in life.

Success.

Money.

Approval.

Pleasure.

They satisfy us for a moment.

But the emptiness eventually returns.

Jesus offers something different.

He offers Himself.

When we know Him, we discover the peace, purpose and hope our hearts have been searching for all along.

Nothing else can truly satisfy the deepest hunger of the human soul.

Only Jesus can.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for sending Jesus to satisfy the deepest needs of my heart.

Help me to seek Him above everything else.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Ask yourself honestly what you've been depending on for happiness.

Invite Jesus to become the centre of your life today.

steps.title: Trusting Jesus Completely

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll see that following Jesus is always worth the cost.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today Jesus invites us into a deeper kind of trust.
steps.teaching_content:
Some people struggled to accept what Jesus was saying.

His words challenged them.

They wanted a Messiah who would fit their expectations.

Instead, Jesus invited them to trust Him completely.

Following Jesus isn't simply agreeing with His teachings.

It is placing your whole life into His hands.

There will be moments when you don't understand everything.

Questions will arise.

Difficulties will come.

Yet faith continues to say,

"I trust Jesus."

Not because every question has been answered.

But because He has proven Himself faithful.

As you continue this journey, remember that your confidence is not in your own understanding.

Your confidence is in Jesus Himself.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Teach me to trust Jesus more each day.

Help me to remain faithful even when I don't understand everything.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Give one unanswered question or concern to God today.

Choose to trust Him, even before you have every answer.

steps.title: Where Else Would We Go?

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover how Jesus brings hope into impossible situations.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today we'll hear one of the most beautiful statements of faith in the Bible.
steps.teaching_content:
Some people stopped following Jesus because His teaching was difficult.

Then Jesus asked His disciples,

"Do you also want to leave?"

Peter answered,

"Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life."

Peter didn't claim to understand everything.

He simply knew there was nowhere else to turn.

That is still true today.

Life offers many voices.

Many promises.

Many alternatives.

But only Jesus offers eternal life.

When life becomes confusing...

When faith feels difficult...

When circumstances don't make sense...

Keep coming back to Jesus.

He alone has the words that lead to life.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You that Jesus is always faithful.

Help me to remain close to Him whatever happens.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Spend a few quiet moments thanking Jesus that He never turns you away.

Choose again today to follow Him.

steps.title: Hope in the Storm

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover the freedom that comes from living for God's approval instead of people's.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today we'll see Jesus meet His disciples in the middle of a storm.
steps.teaching_content:
The disciples were crossing the lake when the wind became strong.

The waves grew higher.

Everything felt uncertain.

Then they saw Jesus walking towards them on the water.

Instead of fear, Jesus spoke peace.

"It is I. Don't be afraid."

Storms come into every life.

Some are obvious.

Others happen quietly inside our hearts.

We worry.

We feel uncertain.

We wonder if God has forgotten us.

But Jesus comes to His people in every storm.

His Presence does not always remove the difficulty immediately.

But it changes everything.

Because when Jesus is with us, we are never alone.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You that Jesus is with me in every storm.

Help me to trust His presence instead of giving in to fear.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Whatever you're facing today, remind yourself that Jesus is with you.

Speak your worries to Him in prayer.

steps.title: Seeking God's Approval

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover the invitation Jesus gives to every thirsty heart.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today Jesus challenges us to think about whose approval matters most.
steps.teaching_content:
The religious leaders were concerned about appearances.

Jesus was concerned about truth.

People often live trying to impress others.

We want acceptance.

Recognition.

Approval.

But living that way becomes exhausting.

Jesus invites us to live differently.

When God becomes the One we seek to please, we are set free from constantly comparing ourselves with everyone else.

His opinion matters most.

He knows your heart.

He knows your struggles.

He knows your desire to follow Him.

As you grow closer to Jesus, you'll discover the freedom that comes from living for an audience of One.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Help me to care more about pleasing You than pleasing people.

Shape my heart to become more like Jesus.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Today, before making an important decision, ask yourself,

"What would honour Jesus most?"

Then choose to follow Him.

steps.title: The Good Shepherd

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll learn to recognise the voice of our Shepherd.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, Jesus tells us something beautiful about the way He cares for us.
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus describes Himself as the Good Shepherd.

A shepherd doesn't watch his sheep from a distance.

He stays close.

He leads them.

Protects them.

Searches for them when they wander.

And knows each one.

Then Jesus says something extraordinary.

The Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.

Jesus isn't simply telling us that He cares.

He's showing us how far His love will go.

All the way to the Cross.

There will be moments when you don't know where life is taking you.

Moments when you feel lost.

Moments when you're afraid.

But you have a Shepherd.

And the One leading you loves you enough to give His life for you.

You don't have to know the whole road ahead.

You simply need to stay close to Him.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for being my Good Shepherd.

Help me to stay close to You and trust You to lead me.

When I feel lost or afraid, remind me that I am never beyond Your care.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Whatever you're facing today, remind yourself:

Jesus is my Shepherd.

I can trust Him to lead me.

steps.title: You Can Trust His Voice

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover that even death is not beyond Jesus' power.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Yesterday, Jesus told us that He is our Good Shepherd.

Today, He reminds us that His sheep know His voice.
steps.teaching_content:
Every day, many voices compete for our attention.

Some tell us what we should fear.

Others tell us what we need to be happy.

Some tell us who we should become.

And sometimes our own thoughts are the loudest voices of all.

Jesus says,

"My sheep hear My Voice."

Following Jesus means learning to recognise His voice among all the others.

We learn His Voice through Scripture.

Through prayer.

Through walking with Him.

And the more we know Him...

The easier it becomes to recognise what sounds like Jesus and what doesn't.

But Jesus makes another promise.

No one can snatch His sheep from His Hand.

You are not holding onto Jesus alone.

Jesus is holding onto you.

Listen for His Voice.

And trust the Hands that are holding you.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Teach me to recognise Your voice.

Help me to listen to You above all the other voices competing for my attention.

Thank You for holding me securely in Your hands.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
As you read Scripture today, don't only ask what the passage means.

Ask:

Jesus, what are You showing me about Yourself?

steps.title: The Resurrection and the Life

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll see what greatness looks like in the Kingdom of God.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, Jesus meets a family in one of life's darkest moments.
steps.teaching_content:
Lazarus had died.

His sisters were grieving.

And Martha couldn't understand why Jesus hadn't arrived sooner.

She said,

"Lord, if You had been here..."

Perhaps you've had moments like that.

Lord, if You had been here...

Why did this happen?

Why didn't You stop it?

Why didn't You answer?

Jesus didn't dismiss Martha's pain.

He met her in it.

Then He said:

"I am the resurrection and the life."

Jesus wasn't simply promising that things would eventually get better.

He was pointing Martha to Himself.

Our hope isn't found in always understanding what God is doing.

Our hope is Jesus.

Even when circumstances seem hopeless...

Jesus is still Lord.

Even death does not have the final word.

He does.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Help me to trust You when I don't understand what is happening.

Thank You that my hope is not in my circumstances.

My hope is in You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Bring something to Jesus today that you don't understand.

You don't need to solve it.

Simply place it in His hands.

steps.title: The Servant King

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover why Jesus can be trusted with our future.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, Jesus does something His disciples never expected.
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus knew who He was.

He knew where He had come from.

He knew where He was going.

And then...

He picked up a towel.

The King knelt down and washed His disciples' feet.

It was the work of a servant.

The disciples were stunned.

But Jesus was showing them what His Kingdom looks like.

Following Jesus isn't about becoming important.

It's about becoming willing to serve.

Jesus didn't only tell His disciples to serve others.

He showed them.

No act of kindness is beneath us.

No person is beneath us.

When we serve someone...

We are walking in the footsteps of Jesus.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for showing me what it means to serve.

Help me to notice the people around me and willingly serve them.

Make my heart more like Yours.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Look for an opportunity to serve someone today.

Don't worry about being noticed.

Just serve.

steps.title: Jesus Is the Way

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover the secret of a life that continues to grow.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, Jesus speaks to His disciples about an uncertain future.
steps.teaching_content:
The disciples were troubled.

Things were changing.

They didn't know what was coming next.

Jesus knew.

And He said,

"Do not let your hearts be troubled."

Then He gave them a reason to trust Him.

"I am the way, the truth and the life."

Jesus didn't hand them a map.

He gave them Himself.

That's important.

Following Jesus doesn't mean you'll always know what's coming next.

Sometimes the road ahead will be unclear.

Sometimes you'll have questions.

Sometimes you won't know what to do.

But Christianity isn't ultimately about knowing the way.

It's about knowing Jesus.

He is the Way.

You may not know what tomorrow holds.

But you can know the One who will walk into tomorrow with you.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

When I don't know what lies ahead, help me to trust You.

Thank You for being the Way, the Truth and the Life.

Lead me as I follow You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Think about something in your future that concerns you.

Give it to Jesus.

Then choose to trust Him with the next step.

steps.title: Stay Close to Jesus

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover the kind of love Jesus wants us to share.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, Jesus gives us a simple picture of what it means to keep growing.
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus said,

"I am the vine; you are the branches."

A branch doesn't struggle to produce life on its own.

It stays connected to the vine.

That's where its life comes from.

Jesus says the same is true for us.

We can try to change ourselves.

Try harder.

Do better.

Become stronger.

But lasting change doesn't begin with trying harder.

It begins with staying close to Jesus.

Jesus calls it remaining in Him.

Talking with Him.

Listening to Him.

Learning His Word.

Trusting Him.

Walking with Him through ordinary life.

And slowly...

His life begins to shape ours.

Following Jesus isn't something you do for a few minutes and then leave behind.

It's a relationship.

Stay close to Jesus.

Let Him produce the change in you.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Help me to remain close to You.

When I begin trying to live this life in my own strength, remind me that I need You.

Let Your life shape mine.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Find a quiet moment today.

Don't ask Jesus for anything.

Simply spend a little time with Him.

steps.title: Love One Another

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover the Helper Jesus promised to send.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, Jesus shows us what His love should begin producing in us.
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus loves you.

We've seen that again and again on this journey.

But His love doesn't stop with you.

Jesus says,

"Love one another as I have loved you."

That's a very different kind of love.

Jesus loved people patiently.

He loved people others ignored.

He forgave.

He served.

He gave.

And ultimately...

He laid down His life.

Following Jesus means allowing His love to change the way we treat people.

Not only the people we like.

Not only the people who treat us well.

Everyone.

Sometimes loving someone will be easy.

Sometimes it won't.

But we don't have to manufacture this love ourselves.

We receive His love...

And then we learn to give it away.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for loving me.

Let Your love change the way I see and treat the people around me.

Help me to love others the way You have loved me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Think of someone who needs to experience kindness today.

Ask Jesus to show you how you can love them well.

Then do it.

steps.title: You Are Not Alone

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll see just how far Jesus' love was willing to go.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, Jesus makes a promise to everyone who follows Him.

You will not walk alone.
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus knew He would soon leave His disciples.

They had walked with Him.

Listened to Him.

Asked Him questions.

Watched Him work.

The thought of life without Jesus must have frightened them.

But Jesus made them a promise.

He would send the Holy Spirit.

A Helper.

A Comforter.

God's Presence with them.

Jesus said,

"I will not leave you as orphans."

Those words still matter.

When you put your faith in Jesus, God doesn't simply forgive you and then leave you to figure everything out.

His Spirit is with you.

Helping you.

Teaching you.

Convicting you.

Comforting you.

Changing you.

There may be times when you feel alone.

But if you belong to Jesus...

You never truly are.
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for giving me Your Holy Spirit.

Help me to become more aware of Your Presence in my everyday life.

Teach me to listen and respond as You lead me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
At some point today, stop what you're doing for a moment.

Quietly remind yourself:

God is with me.

Then ask the Holy Spirit to help you follow Jesus today.

steps.title: Jesus Gave His Life for You

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover why the Cross was not the end.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, we come to the Cross.
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus had healed the sick.

Fed the hungry.

Welcomed outsiders.

Forgiven sinners.

Loved people everyone else had forgotten.

And now...

He was nailed to a Cross.

It looked like defeat.

But something much greater was happening.

Jesus was giving His life.

For us.

For our sin.

For our forgiveness.

For our freedom.

He wasn't forced to the Cross.

He chose it.

That's how seriously God takes sin.

And that's how deeply God loves you.

At the Cross, we see both.

Jesus took what separated us from God...

And opened the way home.

You don't earn that.

You receive it.

Grace brought Jesus to the Cross.

And grace invites you to come near.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for the Cross.

Thank You for giving Your life for me.

Forgive my sin and help me never lose sight of the love You showed there.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Spend a quiet moment thinking about the Cross today.

Simply say:

Jesus, thank You for what You did for me.

steps.title: Jesus Is Alive

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll discover what Jesus does with our doubts.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Yesterday, we stood at the Cross.

Today, everything changes.
steps.teaching_content:
Mary went to the tomb expecting to find a body.

Instead...

The tomb was empty.

Jesus was alive.

Death had not defeated Him.

The grave could not hold Him.

The story wasn't over.

And because Jesus is alive...

Your story doesn't have to end where it is either.

Failure doesn't have the final word.

Sin doesn't have the final word.

Your past doesn't have the final word.

Even death doesn't have the final word.

Jesus does.

Christian faith isn't simply about remembering a man who lived long ago.

Jesus is alive.

He can be known.

He can be followed.

And He is still changing lives today.

Including yours.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You that You are alive.

Thank You that because You live, I can have hope.

Help me to live today knowing that You are with me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a moment today and say these words slowly:

Jesus is alive.

Then ask yourself:

What difference should that make to the way I live today?

steps.title: When You Have Doubts

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll look back at where this journey has brought us.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Today, we meet a disciple who struggled to believe.
steps.teaching_content:
Thomas had questions.

The others told him Jesus was alive.

But Thomas wasn't convinced.

He wanted evidence.

Sometimes people think faith means never having doubts.

But Jesus didn't reject Thomas.

He came to him.

He met Thomas in the middle of his questions.

And invited him to believe.

You may have questions too.

Some may be easy to answer.

Others may take time.

Following Jesus doesn't mean pretending those questions don't exist.

Bring them to Him.

Ask.

Search.

Read Scripture.

Talk with mature followers of Jesus.

Keep walking.

Your questions don't frighten Jesus.

The important thing is what you do with them.

Thomas brought his doubts to Jesus.

And eventually he could say:

"My Lord and my God."
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

You know the things I believe and the things I still struggle to understand.

Help me to bring my questions honestly to You.

Strengthen my faith as I continue walking with You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
If there's something about Jesus or faith that you don't understand, write the question down.

Don't hide it.

Begin looking for the answer.

steps.title: Keep Walking with Jesus

content.closingText: This journey may be complete, but your walk with Jesus is only beginning.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

Thirty days ago, Jesus invited you to come and see.

Today, His invitation continues.
steps.teaching_content:
Peter had failed Jesus.

When Jesus needed him most...

Peter denied even knowing Him.

Three times.

Peter must have wondered whether everything was over.

But after the Resurrection, Jesus came looking for him.

He didn't discard Peter.

He restored him.

And then Jesus said the same words He had spoken near the beginning:

"Follow Me."

That's where these thirty days leave us.

Not at the end.

At the beginning.

You've spent time discovering who Jesus is.

You've seen His compassion.

His power.

His forgiveness.

His Cross.

His Resurrection.

And now the invitation becomes personal.

Follow Me.

There will be good days.

There will be difficult days.

There may even be days when you fail.

Keep coming back to Jesus.

Keep opening Scripture.

Keep praying.

Keep gathering with God's people.

Keep learning.

Keep growing.

Keep walking.

Jesus isn't asking you to know everything today.

He's inviting you to follow Him.

One step at a time.
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for meeting me during these days.

Thank You for Your love, Your grace and Your patience with me.

I want to keep knowing You.

Keep changing me.

Keep leading me.

And help me to follow You wherever You lead.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Don't let this be the end of your time with Jesus.

Choose your next step.

Keep reading His Word.

Keep praying.

Keep walking with Him.

steps.title: Jesus Continues His Work
steps.mentor_intro:
The Gospel of Luke records what Jesus began to do and teach.

The book of Acts shows that His work did not end when He returned to Heaven.

Jesus continued working through His followers in the power of the Holy Spirit.
steps.teaching_content:
Acts is the second part of Luke’s account.

The Gospel of Luke tells us about the earthly life, death and Resurrection of Jesus.

Acts begins with the risen Jesus preparing His disciples for what would happen next.

For forty days, Jesus appeared to them and taught them about the Kingdom of God.

The disciples wanted to know when the kingdom would be restored to Israel.

Jesus directed their attention away from dates and towards their calling.

They were to receive power when the Holy Spirit came upon them.

Then they would become His witnesses.

In Jerusalem.

In Judaea.

In Samaria.

And to the ends of the earth.

This provides the direction for the whole book.

The Good News begins in Jerusalem.

It crosses boundaries into Judaea and Samaria.

It then moves outward through cities, cultures and nations until Paul is proclaiming the Kingdom of God in Rome.

Acts is sometimes called the Acts of the Apostles, but it does not tell us what happened to most of the apostles.

Peter is prominent in the first part.

Paul becomes prominent in the second.

But neither man is the true centre of the story.

Acts records what God continued to do through Jesus Christ, by the power of the Holy Spirit, working in ordinary believers.

Jesus is no longer physically walking through the streets of Jerusalem.

Yet He is still teaching.

Still saving.

Still healing.

Still building His Church.

His followers act in His name, but the power does not come from them.

The mission belongs to Jesus.

The power comes from the Holy Spirit.

The glory belongs to God.

The Ascension did not mark the end of Jesus’ work.

It marked the beginning of the Church’s Spirit-empowered witness to the world.

That same calling continues today.

We have not been asked to stand looking towards Heaven, waiting passively for Jesus to return.

We have been called to live as His witnesses wherever He has placed us.

What does it mean for you to be a witness for Jesus in your present circumstances?

Are you trying to serve Jesus through your own strength, or are you depending upon the Holy Spirit?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You that Your work did not end when You returned to Heaven.

Thank You that You continue to work through Your people.

Fill me with the Holy Spirit.

Give me courage to speak about You and grace to live in a way that reflects You.

Help me remember that the mission belongs to You and that I do not have to fulfil it in my own strength.

Use my life as a faithful witness to Your goodness and salvation.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Think about the people and places that make up your everyday life.

Ask the Holy Spirit to show you how your words, choices and actions can point someone towards Jesus.

steps.title: Filled with the Holy Spirit

content.text:
Jesus promised that His followers would receive power when the Holy Spirit came upon them.

On the Day of Pentecost, that promise was fulfilled.

A frightened group of disciples became a bold, joyful and growing Church.

The disciples obeyed Jesus and waited in Jerusalem.

Then the Holy Spirit came upon them.

There was the sound of a rushing wind.

What appeared to be tongues of fire rested upon them.

They began speaking in other languages as the Holy Spirit enabled them.

Jerusalem was filled with visitors from many nations.

The people heard the followers of Jesus declaring the wonders of God in languages they could understand.

The confusion of languages had once divided people at Babel.

At Pentecost, the Good News began crossing those divisions.

Peter stood and addressed the crowd.

This was the same Peter who had denied knowing Jesus.

Now, filled with the Holy Spirit, he spoke openly and courageously about the crucified and risen Lord.

The Holy Spirit did not draw attention to Himself.

He empowered Peter to point people towards Jesus.

The crowd was deeply convicted and asked what they should do.

Peter called them to repent, be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins and receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

About three thousand people responded.

But Pentecost was not simply a powerful meeting.

It produced a new community.

The believers devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching.

They shared fellowship.

They broke bread together.

They prayed.

They cared for one another.

They shared with those who were in need.

They worshipped God with glad and sincere hearts.

And the Lord continued adding people to their number.

The Church was not built through human enthusiasm alone.

It was born through the work of God.

The Kingdom of God was being proclaimed.

The name of Jesus was being lifted up.

The power of the Holy Spirit was transforming lives.

The wind and fire were unique signs accompanying Pentecost.

But the Church’s continuing need for the Holy Spirit was not temporary.

Acts repeatedly shows believers being filled with the Holy Spirit and receiving courage to speak about Jesus.

The Church still needs His Presence.

We need more than religious activity.

We need the power of the Holy Spirit to help us live as witnesses of Jesus.

What changes do you see in Peter after he is filled with the Holy Spirit?

Which qualities of the first Christian community need to become more visible in the Church today?

Father,

Thank You for the Gift of the Holy Spirit.

Thank You that I do not have to follow Jesus through my own strength.

Fill me with the Holy Spirit.

Give me courage to speak about Jesus.

Create in me a love for Scripture, prayer, fellowship and generosity.

Help Your Church become a community where people encounter the truth, grace and Presence of Jesus.

Amen.

Read Acts 2:42–47 again.

Ask the Holy Spirit to show you which quality of the first Christian community He wants to strengthen in your life.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

steps.mentor_intro:
Jesus promised that His followers would receive power when the Holy Spirit came upon them.

On the Day of Pentecost, that promise was fulfilled.

A frightened group of disciples became a bold, joyful and growing Church.
steps.teaching_content:
The disciples obeyed Jesus and waited in Jerusalem.

Then the Holy Spirit came upon them.

There was the sound of a rushing wind.

What appeared to be tongues of fire rested upon them.

They began speaking in other languages as the Holy Spirit enabled them.

Jerusalem was filled with visitors from many nations.

The people heard the followers of Jesus declaring the wonders of God in languages they could understand.

The confusion of languages had once divided people at Babel.

At Pentecost, the Good News began crossing those divisions.

Peter stood and addressed the crowd.

This was the same Peter who had denied knowing Jesus.

Now, filled with the Holy Spirit, he spoke openly and courageously about the crucified and risen Lord.

The Holy Spirit did not draw attention to Himself.

He empowered Peter to point people towards Jesus.

The crowd was deeply convicted and asked what they should do.

Peter called them to repent, be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins and receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

About three thousand people responded.

But Pentecost was not simply a powerful meeting.

It produced a new community.

The believers devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching.

They shared fellowship.

They broke bread together.

They prayed.

They cared for one another.

They shared with those who were in need.

They worshipped God with glad and sincere hearts.

And the Lord continued adding people to their number.

The Church was not built through human enthusiasm alone.

It was born through the work of God.

The Kingdom of God was being proclaimed.

The name of Jesus was being lifted up.

The power of the Holy Spirit was transforming lives.

The wind and fire were unique signs accompanying Pentecost.

But the Church’s continuing need for the Holy Spirit was not temporary.

Acts repeatedly shows believers being filled with the Holy Spirit and receiving courage to speak about Jesus.

The Church still needs His Presence.

We need more than religious activity.

We need the power of the Holy Spirit to help us live as witnesses of Jesus.

What changes do you see in Peter after he is filled with the Holy Spirit?

Which qualities of the first Christian community need to become more visible in the Church today?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for the Gift of the Holy Spirit.

Thank You that I do not have to follow Jesus through my own strength.

Fill me with the Holy Spirit.

Give me courage to speak about Jesus.

Create in me a love for Scripture, prayer, fellowship and generosity.

Help Your Church become a community where people encounter the truth, grace and Presence of Jesus.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Read Acts 2:42–47 again.

Ask the Holy Spirit to show you which quality of the first Christian community He wants to strengthen in your life.

steps.title: The Gospel Crosses Every Barrier
steps.mentor_intro:
Jesus said that His followers would witness in Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria and to the ends of the earth.

As Acts unfolds, the Good News begins crossing barriers that once separated people.
steps.teaching_content:
The growth of the Church brought new challenges.

In Acts 6, Greek-speaking Jewish widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.

The apostles did not dismiss the complaint.

They recognized that division and unfair treatment could damage the unity and witness of the Church.

Seven trusted, Spirit-filled men were appointed to oversee the practical need.

The result was significant.

The Word of God continued to spread, the number of disciples increased and even many priests became obedient to the faith.

Two of the seven men, Stephen and Philip, went on to play important roles in the expansion of the Gospel.

Stephen was seized because of his witness for Jesus.

Before he was killed, he reminded Israel’s leaders that God had never been confined to one land or one building.

God had spoken and acted beyond the borders of Israel long before the Temple existed.

After Stephen’s death, persecution scattered the believers.

What appeared to be an attempt to stop the Church caused the message to spread even further.

Philip travelled to Samaria and preached about Jesus.

The Samaritans had long been despised by many Jewish people.

Yet they received the Good News with joy.

Philip was then led to an Ethiopian official travelling home from Jerusalem.

Beginning with the passage the man was reading in Isaiah, Philip told him the Good News about Jesus.

The man believed and was baptized.

The Gospel was continuing beyond familiar religious and cultural boundaries.

Then God prepared Peter to enter the home of Cornelius, a Gentile Roman officer.

Peter had to overcome deeply rooted assumptions about who could be welcomed into God’s people.

While Peter was speaking, the Holy Spirit came upon the Gentiles just as He had come upon Jewish believers.

Peter could no longer deny what God had made clear.

God does not show favouritism.

Everyone who turns to Jesus in faith can receive forgiveness and the Holy Spirit.

The Gospel is not the possession of one culture, race, language or social group.

Jesus is Lord of all.

The Church must never build barriers where Jesus has opened a door.

Are there people you may have unconsciously regarded as less likely to receive God’s salvation?

What can the Church learn from the way the apostles responded when the widows were treated unfairly?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You that the Good News of Jesus is for all people.

Forgive me for the barriers I have created through fear, prejudice or habit.

Help me recognize what You are doing in people who are different from me.

Give Your Church the courage to confront unfairness and protect its unity.

Lead us beyond what is comfortable so that more people may hear about Jesus.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Ask God to bring to mind someone whose background, culture or life experience is different from yours.

Pray for that person and choose to treat them with the dignity and welcome that Jesus gives.

steps.title: One Church for All People
steps.mentor_intro:
The conversion of Saul changed the direction of Acts.

The man who tried to destroy the Church became a servant of Jesus and carried the Gospel to the Gentile world.
steps.teaching_content:
Saul was convinced that the followers of Jesus were dangerous.

He approved of Stephen’s death and began travelling from place to place to arrest believers.

Then Jesus met him on the road to Damascus.

A light from Heaven surrounded Saul and he heard Jesus ask why he was persecuting Him.

Saul discovered that attacking the Church meant attacking Jesus Himself.

The risen Jesus was so closely united with His people that He shared in their suffering.

Saul entered Damascus blind and dependent upon others.

Then God spoke to a disciple named Ananias.

Ananias knew Saul’s reputation and was understandably afraid.

Yet he obeyed God, went to Saul and addressed his former enemy as “Brother Saul.”

Saul regained his sight.

He was filled with the Holy Spirit.

He was baptized.

And he began proclaiming that Jesus is the Son of God.

Later, Saul became known as Paul.

The Holy Spirit then spoke to the church in Antioch and told them to set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work to which He had called them.

The church prayed, fasted and sent them out.

Mission did not begin with personal ambition.

It began with the direction of the Holy Spirit and the support of a local church.

As Gentiles began responding to the Gospel, an important disagreement arose.

Some Jewish believers insisted that Gentile converts had to be circumcised and keep the Law of Moses.

The Church gathered in Jerusalem to seek God together.

Peter described how God had given the Holy Spirit to Gentiles through faith.

Paul and Barnabas reported the signs and wonders God had done among them.

James then helped the Church reach a wise and united decision.

Gentile believers would not be required to become Jews in order to follow Jesus.

Salvation comes through the grace of the Lord Jesus.

The decision protected the truth of the Gospel and helped prevent the Church from separating into rival Jewish and Gentile movements.

Unity did not mean avoiding difficult questions.

The believers listened to one another.

They examined what God had done.

They considered Scripture.

And they sought a way forward that preserved both truth and fellowship.

The Church belongs to Jesus.

No culture is permitted to make its customs the doorway into His Kingdom.

What do you learn from Ananias being willing to welcome Saul as a brother?

How did the Church handle disagreement without abandoning truth or unity?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You that Your grace can transform even those who seem furthest from You.

Help me never decide that someone is beyond Your reach.

Give me the courage and obedience of Ananias.

Teach Your Church to face difficult questions with humility, truth and love.

Protect us from division.

Keep us united around Your Gospel and submitted to the leading of the Holy Spirit.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider whether there is someone whose past has made you reluctant to trust that God can change them.

Release that judgement to Jesus and pray for His transforming grace to reach their life.

steps.title: The Word of God Cannot Be Stopped
steps.mentor_intro:
Acts begins with a small group of believers in Jerusalem.

It ends with Paul proclaiming the Kingdom of God in Rome.

Opposition, imprisonment, persecution and distance could not stop the Word of God from spreading.
steps.teaching_content:
The expansion of the Church was directed by the Holy Spirit.

Paul and his companions made plans, but they remained open to God changing their direction.

When the Holy Spirit prevented them from entering certain regions, Paul received a vision calling them into Macedonia.

The Gospel entered a new region, and Lydia became one of the first people there to respond.

Paul usually began his ministry in a city by reasoning from the Scriptures with people who already knew the God of Israel.

But when he spoke in Athens, he addressed people with a very different background.

He began with something they already understood: an altar dedicated to an unknown god.

From there, he told them about the God who created the world and raised Jesus from the dead.

Paul did not change the Gospel.

He changed the starting point so that his hearers could understand it.

Acts shows a consistent missionary pattern.

Believers were sent out under the direction of the Holy Spirit.

They entered significant cities.

They proclaimed the Good News of Jesus.

They made disciples rather than seeking only brief decisions.

They gathered believers into local churches.

They appointed local leaders.

Then they moved on so that the new churches could grow, serve and spread the Gospel themselves.

Paul knew that this calling would involve suffering.

When he spoke to the elders from Ephesus, he said that his life was not his highest concern.

What mattered was completing the work Jesus had given him.

Acts does not present a perfect Church.

There are disagreements, failures, hypocrisy and persecution.

Peter is rescued from prison while James is killed.

Paul and Barnabas experience a sharp disagreement and separate.

Ananias and Sapphira lie to the Holy Spirit.

Acts records both examples to follow and warnings to take seriously.

Yet through every difficulty, the Word of God continues to advance.

By the final chapter, Paul is under house arrest in Rome.

He is chained, but the Gospel is not.

He welcomes people, teaches about the Kingdom of God and speaks about Jesus with boldness.

Acts ends without completing Paul’s story.

The mission is still continuing.

God is still building His Kingdom.

Jesus is still saving people.

The Holy Spirit is still empowering the Church.

And every follower of Jesus is invited to take part.

Are you willing for the Holy Spirit to interrupt your plans and lead you in a different direction?

What would it mean for you to value the calling of Jesus above your comfort or reputation?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You that Your Word cannot be stopped.

Thank You for every person who carried the Good News so that I could hear about Jesus.

Make me sensitive to the direction of the Holy Spirit.

Give me wisdom to communicate the Gospel clearly without changing its truth.

Help me become a faithful disciple who helps others follow Jesus.

Give Your Church courage when opposition comes and humility when mistakes are made.

May Your Kingdom continue to grow through us.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Ask the Holy Spirit where He is sending you as a witness for Jesus.

Be willing to follow His leading, whether that means speaking, serving, welcoming, giving or praying.

steps.title: Acts: Walk Complete

content.text:
You have completed your Walk through the book of Acts.
You have seen the risen Jesus continue His work through ordinary people empowered by the Holy Spirit.
You have watched the Good News move from Jerusalem into Judaea and Samaria, across cultures and nations, and eventually to Rome.
Fearful disciples became courageous witnesses.
People once separated by prejudice became part of one Church.
Those who opposed Jesus were transformed by His grace.
New disciples were formed.
Churches were established.
Leaders were raised.
And through persecution, imprisonment, disagreement and hardship, the Word of God continued to spread.
Acts ends without bringing the mission to a conclusion.
That is because the work is still continuing.
Jesus is still building His Church.
The Holy Spirit is still empowering His people.
The Gospel is still crossing barriers.
And you have been invited to take your place in the story.
Keep following Jesus.
Keep depending upon the Holy Spirit.
Keep living as His witness.

steps.title: A New Beginning

content.text:
Coming to Jesus is more than deciding to become religious.

It's more than adding church, prayer or Bible reading to the life you already have.

The Bible describes something much bigger.

God begins something new.

Paul writes:

"If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!"

That's an extraordinary way to describe what happens when someone comes to Jesus.

A new creation.

It doesn't mean that everything about your life changes overnight.

You may still have struggles.

Old habits may still need to change.

There may be wounds that take time to heal.

You won't suddenly have every question answered.

Following Jesus is a journey of growth.

But something fundamental has changed.

You now belong to Jesus.

Your past no longer has to be the final word over your future.

Your failures don't have to become your identity.

Your sin doesn't have to define your relationship with God.

Because of Jesus, forgiveness is real.

Grace is real.

And new life is possible.

Sometimes we imagine that becoming a Christian means God gives us a long list of things we now have to do.

But the starting point isn't what you do.

It's what God has done.

Jesus has saved you.

And now God begins His work in you.

You will learn.

You will grow.

You will change.

Sometimes that growth will feel exciting.

Sometimes it may feel slow.

There may even be moments when you stumble and wonder whether anything has changed at all.

Don't confuse growth with instant perfection.

A baby is fully alive long before it is fully grown.

In the same way, new life with Jesus begins a process of becoming the person God created you to be.

This is a beginning.

Jesus, thank You for giving me new life.

Thank You that my past doesn't have to define my future.

Help me to understand who I am because of You.

Where there are things in my life that need to change, give me grace and courage to grow.

Teach me to walk with You one step at a time.

Amen.

Consider this question:

What have I allowed from my past to define me?

Perhaps it's a failure.

Something someone did to you.

Something you did.

A label someone gave you.

A regret you still carry.

Bring it honestly to God and remind yourself:

In Jesus, my story isn't finished.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
Following Jesus isn't about becoming perfect overnight.

It's the beginning of new life.
content.lookingAhead:
God hasn't given you new life and then left you to figure everything out alone.

Tomorrow we'll discover an extraordinary promise:

God's Presence goes with you.

steps.title: You Are Not Alone

content.text:
Beginning a new life with Jesus can feel exciting.

It can also feel overwhelming.

How am I supposed to live differently?

How do I change?

How do I follow Jesus when life becomes difficult?

Jesus never intended you to do this alone.

Before Jesus went to the Cross, He prepared His disciples for the fact that He would no longer be physically present with them in the same way.

But He promised them something remarkable.

He would send the Holy Spirit.

Jesus called Him the Advocate, the Helper who would be with them.

God's Presence would remain with His people.

The Holy Spirit isn't simply a feeling or mysterious spiritual force.

He is God's Presence with us.

As you follow Jesus, you don't have to manufacture change through willpower alone.

God is at work in you.

The Holy Spirit helps us understand God's truth.

He reminds us of what Jesus taught.

He convicts us when we're moving away from God's ways.

He strengthens us.

He comforts us.

And over time, He changes us.

There may be moments when you are deeply aware of God's Presence.

There may also be days when you don't feel anything unusual at all.

God's Presence isn't dependent upon your emotions.

You don't have to chase an experience to know that God is with you.

Following Jesus means learning to depend upon God's Presence even in ordinary life.

At work.

At home.

In difficult conversations.

When you're tempted.

When you're afraid.

When you're making decisions.

When life is going well.

And when it isn't.

You are learning to walk with God.

And you are not walking alone.

Holy Spirit, thank You for God's Presence in my life.

Help me to recognise Your Work in me.

Teach me to listen when You correct me, depend upon You when I am weak, and trust You when I don't know what to do.

Help me remember that I don't have to follow Jesus in my own strength.

Amen.

During your ordinary day, remind yourself:

God is with me here.

You don't need to create a special spiritual moment.

At work, at home, while travelling or sitting quietly, simply become aware that following Jesus includes God's Presence in everyday life.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
Jesus didn't call you to follow Him alone.

God's Presence goes with you.
content.lookingAhead:
Relationships grow when people spend time together.

Your relationship with God does too.

Tomorrow we'll begin discovering two simple ways of growing in that relationship:

Listening to God and talking with Him.

steps.title: Learning to Know God

content.text:
Think about any close relationship in your life.

You didn't build it by meeting someone once and then never speaking again.

Relationships grow through connection.

Knowing God is no different.

Jesus told His disciples:

"Remain in me, as I also remain in you."

He used the picture of a branch connected to a vine.

A branch doesn't produce life by trying harder.

It receives life by remaining connected.

That's a helpful picture of our relationship with Jesus.

Christian growth isn't simply about trying harder to behave like a Christian.

It grows out of staying connected to Jesus.

Two important ways we learn to do that are through Scripture and prayer.

The Bible allows us to discover who God is, what He has done and how He calls us to live.

We don't read Scripture merely to collect information.

We read because we want to know God.

Prayer is the other side of that relationship.

God speaks through His Word.

We respond to Him in prayer.

Prayer doesn't require special language.

You can talk to God honestly.

Tell Him when you're grateful.

Tell Him when you're afraid.

Tell Him when you're angry.

Ask questions.

Ask for help.

Confess when you've done something wrong.

Sometimes you may have lots to say.

Sometimes you may simply sit quietly in God's Presence.

Don't turn Bible reading and prayer into a test of whether you're a good enough Christian.

They're invitations.

God invites you to know Him.

And relationships grow through connection.

God, I want to know You more.

Give me a desire for Your Word and help me understand what I read.

Teach me to pray honestly rather than trying to find impressive words.

Help me remain connected to Jesus and allow my relationship with You to grow.

Amen.

Open a passage of Scripture today.

Read it slowly.

Then ask two simple questions:

What does this show me about God?

What might God be saying to me through this?

Then talk to Him about your answer.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
Scripture and prayer aren't religious tasks to complete.

They're part of learning to know God.
content.lookingAhead:
Your relationship with God is personal.

But it was never intended to become private.

Tomorrow we'll discover that when you come to Jesus, you become part of something bigger than yourself.

You belong to a family.

content.text:
Following Jesus is deeply personal.

Nobody else can trust Him for you.

But following Jesus was never intended to become something you do entirely on your own.

When you come to Jesus, you become part of a family.

When the first people began following Jesus, they didn't simply return home and practise their new faith alone.

They gathered.

They learned together.

They ate together.

They prayed together.

They shared life.

This community of Jesus-followers became what the Bible calls the Church.

The Church isn't primarily a building.

It isn't a Sunday programme.

And it isn't simply an organisation.

The Church is people.

People who belong to Jesus and are learning to follow Him together.

Church communities aren't perfect.

They're filled with imperfect people who are still growing.

Sometimes people in Church will disappoint you.

Sometimes you may disappoint them.

But God still designed the Christian life to be lived in community.

We need people who can encourage us.

Teach us.

Pray with us.

Challenge us.

Celebrate with us.

Walk through difficult seasons with us.

And we have something to give them too.

You aren't only joining a community because of what you can receive.

God will also use you to encourage, love and serve others.

This is why gathering with other believers matters.

You don't have to know everything before you belong.

You don't have to become spiritually mature first.

You are joining a family of people who are all learning to follow Jesus.

Together.

God, thank You that I don't have to follow Jesus alone.

Help me to find my place among Your people.

Give me relationships with people who will encourage me, teach me and help me grow.

And show me how I can encourage, love and serve others too.

Help Your Church increasingly reflect the love and character of Jesus.

Amen.

Think about your connection with other followers of Jesus.

Do you have a Church community where you can grow, worship and build relationships?

If you do, consider how you can move from simply attending to genuinely belonging.

If you don't, ask God to lead you toward a healthy Church community where Jesus and Scripture are central.

But you were never meant to walk alone.
content.lookingAhead:

God's Presence is with you.

You're learning to know Him.

And you belong to His people.

Now comes the everyday adventure:

Learning to actually follow Jesus.

steps.title: Following Jesus One Step at a Time

content.text:
When Jesus met people, His invitation was wonderfully simple:

"Follow Me."

He didn't say:

"Understand everything first."

He invited them to begin walking with Him.

Following Jesus is more than believing that He exists.

It's more than attending Church.

And it's more than having a moment when you decided to trust Him.

It's a life of discipleship.

A disciple is someone who learns from and follows another person.

Jesus invites us to learn His ways and increasingly allow Him to shape how we live.

That happens one step at a time.

You'll discover things in Scripture that challenge you.

There will be habits that need to change.

There may be relationships that need healing.

There will be moments when following Jesus means choosing His way when another way seems easier.

Sometimes you'll get it right.

Sometimes you won't.

When you stumble, don't assume the journey is over.

Come back to Jesus.

Receive His grace.

Learn.

Get up.

Keep walking.

Following Jesus isn't about proving to God how committed you are.

It's responding to the One who already loved you enough to go to the Cross for you.

Jesus speaks about taking up our Cross and following Him.

That means He isn't simply an addition to our plans.

We learn to surrender our lives to Him.

Our decisions.

Our relationships.

Our priorities.

Our ambitions.

Our time.

Our future.

That may sound enormous.

And over a lifetime, it is.

But you don't have to live your entire Christian life today.

You only need to take the next step with Jesus.

Then another.

Then another.

That's discipleship.

A lifetime of learning to walk with Him.

Jesus, thank You for inviting me to follow You.

I don't have everything figured out.

There are things I still need to learn and areas where I still need to grow.

Help me to trust You enough to follow Your way.

When I stumble, teach me to return to You rather than run from You.

Shape my life as I learn to walk with You one step at a time.

Amen.

Ask Jesus a simple question:

What is my next step with You?

Perhaps something immediately comes to mind.

Perhaps it doesn't.

Either way, remain open.

Following Jesus isn't about knowing every step of the journey in advance.

It's about trusting the One you're following.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You don't have to have the whole journey figured out.

Keep following Jesus.

One step at a time.
content.lookingAhead:

But how does that relationship grow through ordinary days, changing seasons, difficult decisions, joy, disappointment and everything else life brings?

That's where we're going next.

The final Walk in Come and See is:

Walking with God.

steps.title: Your New Life Has Begun

content.text:
You've completed Beginning Your New Life.

But this isn't really an ending.

It's a beginning.

You've discovered that coming to Jesus means more than adding Christianity to your old life.

God begins something new.

Your past doesn't have to define your future.

God's Presence is with you.

You can grow in your relationship with Him through Scripture and prayer.

You belong among God's people.

And Jesus invites you to follow Him one step at a time.

There will still be things you don't understand.

There will be areas where you need to grow.

There will be wonderful moments when God's work in your life seems obvious.

And there may be seasons when growth feels slow.

You will have victories.

You may stumble.

When you do, don't hide from God.

Come back to Him.

Remember what we've already discovered: when humanity hid, God came looking.

The Christian life isn't about proving that you're good enough to belong to Jesus.

You belong to Him because of what He has done for you.

Now you get to learn what it means to live with Him.

Not only at Church.

Not only when you're reading the Bible.

Not only when you're praying.

But in ordinary life.

At home.

At work.

In your relationships.

In your decisions.

In your joys.

In your disappointments.

Jesus isn't inviting you merely to believe in Him.

He's inviting you to walk with Him.

And that journey lasts a lifetime.
