steps.title: Jesus Is Supreme
steps.mentor_intro:
The believers in Colosse were being exposed to ideas that lowered their view of Jesus.

Paul brings them back to the truth.

Jesus is not one spiritual power among many.

He is Lord over all.
steps.teaching_content:
Colosse was surrounded by many religious beliefs.

People feared spiritual powers in nature.

Some looked to astrology for guidance.

Others worshipped Greek and Roman gods.

Some believed that secret knowledge or strict religious practices could help them reach spiritual fullness.

These ideas began influencing the church.

The believers did not necessarily reject Jesus.

Instead, they began adding other spiritual ideas and practices to their faith.

Jesus was still present, but He was no longer central.

Paul responds by giving them one of the clearest descriptions of Jesus in the New Testament.

Jesus is the visible Image of the invisible God.

Everything was created through Him.

Everything was created for Him.

He existed before all things.

Everything is held together in Him.

Jesus is not part of creation.

He is its Creator and Lord.

He is also the Head of the Church.

No human leader, spiritual being or religious system can take His place.

All the fullness of God dwells in Jesus.

We do not need another spiritual mediator to bring us closer to God.

When we come to Jesus, we come to the One in whom all God’s fullness is found.

Jesus is also the One through whom God reconciles us to Himself.

Sin made us enemies of God in our minds and behaviour.

Through the physical death of Jesus on the Cross, God opened the way for us to be brought back into relationship with Him.

The Cross was not only an example of sacrificial love.

Through the Cross, Jesus dealt with our guilt and defeated the powers that held us in fear.

Paul calls the believers to continue in their faith.

They must remain established and firm without moving away from the hope of the Gospel.

Beginning with Jesus is not enough if we later move Him to the edge of our lives.

We must continue trusting Him.

Everything we need for salvation and life with God is found in Jesus.

He is Creator.

Sustainer.

Saviour.

Head of the Church.

Lord over every power.

Jesus is enough.

Have other beliefs, fears or spiritual practices begun competing with Jesus for your trust?

Is Jesus simply part of your life, or is He truly Lord over everything?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

You are the Image of the invisible God.

Everything was created through You and for You.

Thank You for reconciling me to the Father through the Cross.

Forgive me for allowing other fears, beliefs or desires to compete with You.

Take Your rightful place at the centre of my life.

Keep me rooted and established in the Gospel.

Teach me to trust that You are completely sufficient.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider whether you are looking to anything besides Jesus for spiritual security, identity or guidance.

Bring it under His Lordship and reaffirm your trust in Him.

steps.title: Complete in Christ
steps.mentor_intro:
The Colossians had received Jesus as Lord.

Now they needed to continue living in Him without being captured by ideas that suggested Jesus was not enough.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul urges the believers to continue in the same Jesus they originally received.

They are to be rooted in Him.

Built up in Him.

Strengthened in faith.

Overflowing with gratitude.

The danger was that persuasive ideas would carry them away from Jesus.

Some teachers offered spiritual fullness through philosophy, mystical experiences, strict rules and the worship of angels.

They made God appear distant and filled the space between God and humanity with other spiritual beings and practices.

Paul responds with a clear truth.

All the fullness of God lives bodily in Jesus.

And believers have been brought to fullness in Him.

Nothing needs to be added.

Jesus is the Head over every power and authority.

Through faith, believers are united with His death and Resurrection.

The old life is buried with Him.

A new life begins through the power of God.

We were spiritually dead because of sin.

God made us alive with Jesus.

He forgave our sins and cancelled the record of debt that stood against us.

At the Cross, Jesus disarmed the spiritual powers and triumphed over them.

Because of this, believers must not allow anyone to condemn them over food, religious festivals or special days.

These things cannot give us new life.

Nor should we become obsessed with visions, angels or spiritual experiences that draw attention away from Jesus.

Strict rules can appear wise and disciplined.

“Do not handle.”

“Do not taste.”

“Do not touch.”

But external regulations cannot transform the desires of the heart.

Christianity is not about controlling the old life through more religious rules.

It is about sharing in the new life of Jesus.

Some people seek spiritual fullness through rituals.

Others seek it through mystical experiences, secret knowledge or borrowed spiritual practices.

Paul points us back to Jesus.

We do not need to search elsewhere for what God has already given us in His Son.

We are not made complete by adding more religion to Jesus.

We are complete in Christ.

Are there religious rules or spiritual practices that make you feel more acceptable to God than other believers?

Are you seeking somewhere else for something God has already given you in Jesus?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You that all Your fullness is found in Jesus.

Thank You for making me alive with Him and forgiving all my sins.

Thank You that the Cross has cancelled my debt and defeated the powers of darkness.

Protect me from ideas and practices that draw my attention away from Jesus.

Free me from empty religion and fear-based rules.

Help me remain rooted, strengthened and complete in Christ.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Examine one religious habit or spiritual practice in your life.

Ask whether it genuinely helps you remain close to Jesus or whether it has become a substitute for trusting Him.

steps.title: Put On the New Life
steps.mentor_intro:
New life in Jesus must become visible in the way we think, speak and relate to others.

Paul calls believers to put off the old life and put on the character of Christ.
steps.teaching_content:
Those who belong to Jesus have been raised with Him.

Their hearts and minds must now be directed towards the things of God.

This does not mean ignoring ordinary life.

It means allowing the reality of Jesus to reshape ordinary life.

Paul tells believers to put to death the attitudes and behaviours of the old life.

Sexual immorality.

Impurity.

Lust.

Evil desires.

Greed.

Anger.

Rage.

Malice.

Slander.

Abusive speech.

Lying.

These things do not belong to the new person Jesus is forming.

The Christian life requires deliberate choices.

We put off what belongs to the old self.

Then we put on what reflects Jesus.

Compassion.

Kindness.

Humility.

Gentleness.

Patience.

We bear with one another.

We forgive because the Lord has forgiven us.

Above everything else, we put on love.

Love binds all the other qualities together in unity.

The peace of Jesus must govern our relationships.

His Word must dwell richly among us.

Worship, gratitude, teaching and encouragement should fill the life of the Church.

Whatever we say or do should be done in the name of Jesus.

This new life reaches into the home.

Wives and husbands must allow their relationship to come under the Lordship of Jesus.

Husbands are called to love rather than become harsh.

Children are called to obey.

Parents must not crush or discourage their children.

The new life also changes working relationships.

Believers should work sincerely, not merely when someone is watching.

Those with authority must act fairly, remembering that they also answer to the Lord.

Paul ends by calling believers to prayer and wise witness.

We are to remain watchful and thankful in prayer.

We should ask God to open doors for the Gospel.

Our behaviour towards outsiders must be wise.

Our words should be gracious and appropriate to the person before us.

Jesus does not only change what we believe.

He changes our character, homes, work, speech and witness.

We do not simply begin with Christ.

We continue living in Him until His character becomes visible in every part of life.

What attitude or behaviour from the old life do you need to put off?

Which part of the character of Jesus do you most need to put on?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You for giving me new life.

Help me put to death the attitudes and desires that belong to my old way of living.

Clothe me with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.

Teach me to forgive as You have forgiven me.

Let Your love and peace govern my relationships.

May Your Word dwell richly within me.

Shape my home, work, speech and witness so that everything I do honours You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Identify one old attitude to put off and one Christlike quality to put on.

Ask the Holy Spirit to help you practise that change in your next interaction with someone.

steps.title: Made in God's Image

content.text:
There are many ways people answer the question:

Who am I?

We often define ourselves by our family, our work, our relationships, our successes—or even our failures.

But the Bible begins somewhere deeper.

Before anything you've done, achieved or experienced, God says something remarkable about humanity:

We were created in His Image.

When God created the heavens and the earth, He created an extraordinary variety of life.

But when the story reaches humanity, something changes.

God says:

"Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness."

Human beings have a unique place in God's creation.

Being made in God's image doesn't mean that God has a human body and we physically look like Him.

It means that God created humanity to reflect something of who He is.

We can think.

Create.

Love.

Choose.

Communicate.

Build relationships.

Recognise right and wrong.

And God gave humanity responsibility within His creation.

There's something else important here.

Genesis doesn't say that only certain people carry God's image.

It says:

"Male and female he created them."

The image of God isn't something you earn.

It doesn't belong only to people who are successful, intelligent, wealthy, powerful or religious.

It is part of God's intention for humanity.

And that gives us a very different starting point for understanding ourselves.

Your deepest identity isn't found in your job.

Your possessions.

Your achievements.

Your failures.

Your past.

Or what somebody else has said about you.

Before any of those things entered your story:

You were created by God.

That doesn't mean humanity now perfectly reflects God's image. Something went terribly wrong—and we'll eventually have to talk about that.

But before we talk about what went wrong, we need to understand what God intended.

Human beings were created with extraordinary dignity and significance.

Including you.

God, thank You for creating me.

Help me to understand what it means to be made in Your image.

Where I have allowed my identity to be defined by my achievements, failures, circumstances or the opinions of others, help me to see myself from Your perspective.

Teach me what You intended when You created humanity.

Amen.

Consider this question:

What have I allowed to define who I am?

Perhaps it's something you've achieved.

Something you've failed at.

Something somebody said about you.

Your family.

Your work.

Your past.

You don't have to resolve all of that today.

Simply begin with this truth:

I was created by God and made in His Image.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
Your story doesn't begin with what you've done.

It begins with the God who created you.

steps.title: Created with Purpose

content.text:
Yesterday we discovered that human beings were created in God's image.

But Genesis doesn't stop there.

God didn't create humanity simply to exist.

He gave us purpose.

One of life's biggest questions is:

Why am I here?

We often try to answer that question by looking at what we do.

Our career.

Our family.

Our abilities.

Our achievements.

Our dreams.

Those things can certainly become part of our purpose, but the Bible takes us further back.

When God created humanity, He gave them responsibility within His creation.

They were to care for what God had made, develop it, cultivate it and exercise the authority He had entrusted to them.

In other words, humanity wasn't created merely to occupy space.

We were created to participate in God's purposes.

That gives work, creativity, relationships, service and responsibility significance.

Purpose isn't only something reserved for pastors, missionaries or people doing obviously "religious" things.

God created human beings to represent Him wherever He places them.

That means your life matters to God.

Your abilities matter.

The way you treat people matters.

The way you work matters.

What you do with what God has entrusted to you matters.

But there's an important distinction.

Your purpose gives direction to what you do.

It doesn't determine your value.

You were made in God's image before you accomplished anything.

So you don't have to spend your life achieving things in order to prove that you matter.

Instead, you can begin asking a different question:

Not simply,

"What do I want to do with my life?"

but,

"God, what did You create my life for?"

You may not know the complete answer yet.

That's okay.

Purpose isn't always discovered in one dramatic moment.

Often it unfolds as we learn to know God, recognise what He has entrusted to us, and faithfully walk with Him.

God, thank You that my life isn't without meaning or purpose.

Help me to understand why You created me and what You have entrusted to me.

Teach me to use my abilities, opportunities, relationships and responsibilities in ways that honour You.

Lead me as I discover more of Your purpose for my life.

Amen.

Think about what God has already placed in your hands.

Your abilities.

Your relationships.

Your opportunities.

Your responsibilities.

Instead of asking whether they are important enough, ask:

How can I honour God with what He has already entrusted to me?

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You weren't created merely to exist.

You were created with purpose.
content.lookingAhead:
God created us in His image and gave us purpose.

But He didn't create us to live that purpose alone.

From the beginning, humanity was created for relationship—with God and with one another.

That's where we're going next.

steps.title: Created for Relationship

content.text:
God created us in His image.

He created us with purpose.

But there is another part of God's design that we cannot miss.

We were created for relationship.

With God.

And with one another.

There is an interesting moment in the creation story.

Again and again, God looks at what He has made and declares it good.

Then, for the first time, God says:

"It is not good..."

What wasn't good?

The man was alone.

God had created Adam. He had given him a place to live and meaningful work to do.

But something was missing.

Relationship.

God created Eve, and human community began.

This tells us something important about God's design for us:

We were never created to walk through life completely alone.

We need other people.

Friendship.

Family.

Community.

People who know us.

People we can love, encourage, support and serve.

But even our relationships with one another aren't the deepest relationship we were created for.

Humanity was also created to know God.

In the beginning, Adam and Eve lived in relationship with their Creator.

God wasn't simply an idea they believed in.

He wasn't a distant being somewhere beyond their world.

They knew Him.

This helps us understand something about ourselves.

There is a longing in human beings that achievements, possessions and even other people can never completely satisfy.

We can have success and still feel empty.

We can be surrounded by people and still feel alone.

We can have almost everything we thought we wanted and still wonder:

"Is this all there is?"

Perhaps that's because we were created for more.

We were created to know the One who made us.

And we were created to share life with others.

This is why following Jesus was never intended to become a completely private journey between "me and God."

God draws us to Himself, but He also draws us into community.

We learn together.

We encourage one another.

We carry one another through difficult seasons.

We celebrate together.

We worship together.

We walk together.

You were created for relationship.

With God and with people.

God, thank You that You created me to know You.

Thank You also for the people You have placed around me.

Teach me to grow in my relationship with You and to build relationships that reflect Your love.

Where I've withdrawn, become isolated or tried to walk through life entirely on my own, help me to recognise the gift of community.

Amen.

Think about the relationships in your life.

Who has God placed around you?

Who encourages you?

Who might need encouragement from you?

And then consider your relationship with God.

Don't only think about Him today.

Talk to Him.

Relationship grows through connection.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You weren't created simply to believe that God exists.

You were created to know Him—and you were never meant to walk alone.
content.lookingAhead:
If every human being has been created in God's image, then this truth doesn't only change the way we see ourselves.

It changes the way we see everyone else.

Next we'll explore why every person has value.

steps.title: Every Person Has Value

content.text:
We've discovered that we were created in God's image, with purpose and for relationship.

But being made in God's image doesn't only tell us something about ourselves.

It tells us something about every person we meet.

Every human life has value because every human being has been created by God.

Our world has many ways of deciding how much a person matters.

We value people because of what they can do.

What they own.

How successful they are.

How intelligent they are.

How they look.

How influential they are.

Sometimes we even measure our own worth in exactly the same ways.

But God gives human value a very different foundation.

Every person is created in His image.

That means human worth isn't something we achieve.

It isn't something another person gives us.

And it isn't something another person has the authority to take away.

A newborn baby who has achieved nothing carries the image of God.

An elderly person who can no longer do what they once could carries the image of God.

The person with extraordinary abilities carries God's image.

So does the person whose abilities the world may overlook.

The wealthy.

The poor.

The powerful.

The forgotten.

The person you admire.

And even the person you find difficult to love.

Every one of them matters to God.

This truth should change two things.

First, it changes the way you see yourself.

Your worth doesn't disappear when you fail.

It isn't increased when people applaud you or decreased when they reject you.

Your value begins with the God who created you.

Second, it changes the way you see other people.

We cannot claim to honour God while treating people made in His image as though they have no value.

The person serving you.

The person working for you.

The stranger you pass.

The person who cannot give you anything in return.

The person whose life looks completely different from yours.

All deserve to be treated with dignity.

This doesn't mean everything people do is right.

Being made in God's image doesn't remove accountability or make every human choice good.

It means that even when we disagree with someone's choices or behaviour, we must never forget that we're dealing with a person God created.

Imagine how different our families, churches, workplaces and communities could become if we genuinely learned to see people this way.

God, thank You for creating every person in Your image.

Help me to see myself as You see me and to recognise the dignity You have given me.

And help me to see Your image in the people around me.

Forgive me for the times I've judged someone's worth by their appearance, achievements, background or usefulness to me.

Teach me to treat people with the dignity, compassion and respect that reflect Your heart.

Amen.

Think about someone you might easily overlook, dismiss or judge.

Then remind yourself:

This person was created in the image of God.

Allow that truth to shape the way you see and treat them.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
Human value isn't something we give to one another.

It begins with the God who created us in His Image.
content.lookingAhead:
We've discovered something extraordinary about God's original design for humanity.

Created in His image.

Created with purpose.

Created for relationship.

Created with value.

Tomorrow we'll bring these truths together and ask:

What does it mean to actually live as someone created in God's Image?

steps.title: Living as God's Image-Bearer

content.text:
Over the past few days, we've discovered something remarkable about God's design for humanity.

We were created in His image.

Created with purpose.

Created for relationship.

And created with dignity and value.

Today we bring those truths together.

Because being made in God's Image isn't only something to understand.

It should shape the way we live.

If you were created to reflect something of who God is, then an important question follows:

What does that look like in everyday life?

It begins with knowing God.

The more we discover His character, the more we begin to understand what our lives were intended to reflect.

God is loving.

So we learn to love.

God is merciful.

So we learn to show mercy.

God is faithful.

So we become people others can trust.

God cares about justice.

So we care when people are treated unfairly.

God forgives.

So we learn the difficult work of forgiveness.

God is generous.

So His generosity begins shaping ours.

This doesn't mean we become God.

And it certainly doesn't mean we will reflect Him perfectly.

We won't.

But it does mean that our lives were created to point beyond ourselves toward the One whose image we bear.

Paul tells followers of Jesus to clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.

That's a beautiful picture.

Every morning we choose what clothes we're going to wear.

Paul says there is another kind of clothing that should increasingly become visible in our lives.

The character of God.

And notice how practical it becomes.

Being God's image-bearer affects the way you speak to your family.

The way you treat someone who cannot do anything for you.

The way you respond when someone hurts you.

The way you use your abilities.

The way you handle responsibility.

The way you see yourself.

The way you see other people.

The way you live when nobody is watching.

Christianity isn't simply about believing the correct things about God.

God wants His work in us to begin changing the people we become.

There is a problem, though.

When we look honestly at ourselves—and at the world around us—we quickly realise that humanity doesn't reflect God the way we were created to.

We hurt one another.

We become selfish.

We lie.

We hate.

We exploit.

We destroy.

We choose our own way instead of God's.

Something has gone terribly wrong.

That doesn't erase the value God placed upon humanity.

But it does mean that we need more than advice about becoming better people.

We need God to restore what has been broken.

And that's where the story is heading.

God, thank You for creating me in Your image.

Help me not only to understand what that means, but to allow that truth to shape the way I live.

Teach me to reflect Your love, kindness, mercy, faithfulness and goodness in the way I treat others.

Show me the areas of my life that don't reflect Your character, and continue Your work in me.

Amen.

Ask yourself:

What might it look like for my life to reflect God's character today?

Don't try to change everything at once.

Simply pay attention to the people and situations already in front of you, and ask God to help you respond in a way that reflects Him.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You were created in God's Image.

Not merely to know something about yourself—

but to live in a way that points toward Him.
content.lookingAhead:
God's original design was good.

Humanity was created in His image, with purpose, for relationship and to reflect His character.

But when we look at our world—and when we're honest about ourselves—we know this isn't the whole story.

Something went wrong.

The next part of our journey asks the question we cannot avoid:

If God created humanity good, why is our world so broken?

Next, we'll explore What Went Wrong?

That doesn't erase the value God placed upon humanity.

But it does mean that we need more than advice about becoming better people.

We need God to restore what has been broken.

And that's where the story is heading.
steps.prayer:
God, thank You for creating me in Your image.

Help me not only to understand what that means, but to allow that truth to shape the way I live.

Teach me to reflect Your love, kindness, mercy, faithfulness and goodness in the way I treat others.

Show me the areas of my life that don't reflect Your character, and continue Your work in me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Ask yourself:

What might it look like for my life to reflect God's character today?

Don't try to change everything at once.

Simply pay attention to the people and situations already in front of you, and ask God to help you respond in a way that reflects Him.

steps.title: Created with Purpose. Created with Value.

content.text:
You've completed Created in God's Image.

Over these five days, you've discovered something important about God's original design for humanity.

You were created by God.

You were made in His image.

You were created with purpose.

You were created for relationship—with God and with others.

And because every person bears God's image, every human life has dignity and value.

These aren't simply ideas to learn.

They change the way we see ourselves.

They change the way we see other people.

And they begin changing the way we live.

Your identity isn't ultimately determined by what you've achieved, what you've failed at, what you own, what you've experienced, or what somebody else has said about you.

Your story begins with your Creator.

You were created by God and for God.

But we've also reached an uncomfortable part of the story.

When we look at ourselves and our world, it's obvious that humanity isn't living according to God's original design.

Something has gone wrong.

Understanding what happened will help us understand why our world is broken—and ultimately why we need Jesus.

That's where we're going next.

steps.title: Blessed in Christ
steps.mentor_intro:
Ephesians begins with worship.

Before Paul tells believers how to live, he reminds them of everything God has done for them through Jesus.

Christian behaviour begins with Christian identity.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul opens his letter with a long expression of praise.

God has blessed His people with every spiritual blessing in Christ.

He chose us in Christ.

He adopted us into His family.

He redeemed us through the Blood of Jesus.

He forgave our sins.

He revealed His purpose.

He gave us the Holy Spirit.

Again and again, Paul uses the words “in Christ.”

Every blessing is found in Him.

God’s purpose reaches further back than our first response to the Gospel.

Before the creation of the world, He planned to form a people who would belong to Jesus and become holy in His Presence.

This does not make us unthinking objects without a choice.

God reveals His grace and calls us to respond through faith.

We must continue trusting Jesus and allow God to accomplish His purpose within us.

God’s plan is greater than the salvation of isolated individuals.

His purpose is to bring everything in Heaven and on earth together under Jesus Christ.

The world is divided by sin.

People are separated from God and from one another.

Creation itself is broken.

But God is working towards a day when everything will be brought under the rightful rule of Jesus.

The Holy Spirit is God’s seal upon those who believe.

His Presence is a deposit guaranteeing the inheritance God has promised.

We do not yet experience the fullness of everything God has prepared, but the Holy Spirit assures us that we belong to Him.

Paul then prays for the believers.

He does not only ask that they receive more information.

He asks that the eyes of their hearts be opened.

He wants them to know the hope of God’s calling, the riches of their inheritance and the greatness of His power.

This is the same power that raised Jesus from the dead and seated Him above every rule, authority, power and dominion.

Jesus is not competing with the spiritual powers.

He is above them.

He is Lord over everything.

And God has made Him Head of the Church.

The Christian life begins by understanding who Jesus is, what He has done and who we have become in Him.

Is your identity shaped more by your past, achievements and failures, or by who you are in Christ?

Which spiritual blessing in Ephesians 1 do you most need to receive with confidence?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for every blessing You have given me in Jesus.

Thank You for choosing me in Christ, adopting me into Your family and forgiving my sins.

Open the eyes of my heart.

Help me understand the hope of Your calling and the greatness of Your power.

Fill me with the Holy Spirit and keep my life firmly rooted in Jesus.

May Your purpose be fulfilled in me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Read Ephesians 1:3–14 again.

Notice every phrase describing what God has done for you in Christ and thank Him personally for each one.

steps.title: Saved for Good Works
steps.mentor_intro:
Christianity is not about becoming good enough for God to accept us.

God accepts us through Jesus and then begins making us into the people He created us to be.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul describes the condition from which Jesus saves us.

We were spiritually dead in sin.

We followed the patterns of the world.

We were influenced by spiritual evil.

We lived according to desires that pulled us away from God.

A spiritually dead person cannot rescue themselves.

Then Paul introduces the turning point.

“But God.”

God is rich in mercy.

Because of His great love, He made us alive with Jesus even when we were dead in sin.

He raised us with Christ and gave us a new position in Him.

Salvation begins with what God has done, not what we have achieved.

We are saved by grace through faith.

Grace is God giving us what we could never earn.

Faith receives what grace provides.

Even faith does not become something about which we can boast.

Salvation is God’s gift.

Good works cannot save us.

But that does not mean good works are unimportant.

We are not saved by good works.

We are saved for good works.

God is not only rescuing us from judgement.

He is restoring His Image within us and preparing us to live differently.

We are God’s workmanship.

He is forming our lives according to His purpose.

He has prepared good works for us to walk in.

This order is essential.

Religion tells us to become good enough so that God might accept us.

The Gospel tells us that God welcomes us through Jesus so that He can transform us.

Christian duty flows from Christian identity.

Obedience is not an attempt to purchase God’s love.

It is our response to the love we have already received.

Grace does not produce passivity.

It produces a new life.

God saves us so that His goodness, mercy and character may become visible through us.

Are you still trying to earn the acceptance that God offers freely through Jesus?

What good work may God have placed before you as an opportunity to reflect His character?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for Your rich mercy and great love.

Thank You for making me alive with Jesus.

I confess that I could never save myself.

Thank You that salvation is Your gift of grace.

Free me from striving to earn Your acceptance.

Continue shaping me as Your workmanship.

Help me walk in the good works You have prepared and let my life reflect Your goodness.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Approach something good God has placed before you as a response to grace, not as an attempt to earn His love.

Serve willingly because you already belong to Him.

steps.title: One New Family
steps.mentor_intro:
The Gospel does more than reconcile individuals to God.

Through Jesus, people who were once separated from one another are brought together as one family.
steps.teaching_content:
The division between Jews and Gentiles was deep.

Gentiles had been excluded from Israel’s Covenants and promises.

They were without hope and without God in the world.

The Temple in Jerusalem contained a physical barrier preventing Gentiles from entering the inner courts.

That wall represented generations of spiritual, cultural and social separation.

But Jesus changed everything.

Those who were far away have been brought near through His Blood.

Jesus Himself is our peace.

Through the Cross, He destroyed the hostility and created one new humanity from Jews and Gentiles.

Both now have access to the Father through the same Holy Spirit.

Gentile believers are no longer foreigners and outsiders.

They are fellow citizens with God’s people.

They belong to God’s household.

The Church is pictured as a new Temple.

Jesus is the Cornerstone.

The apostles and prophets form the foundation.

Every believer is joined together as part of a dwelling in which God lives through the Holy Spirit.

God’s Presence is no longer associated with one building or restricted by a dividing wall.

He lives among His people.

Paul describes this as a mystery.

In Scripture, a mystery is not something that remains impossible to understand.

It is something once hidden that God has now revealed.

The mystery is that Gentiles share equally in God’s promise through Jesus.

The Church displays this wisdom of God not only to the world but also to spiritual rulers and authorities.

When people who were once separated live together in Christ, they reveal the power of the Gospel.

Paul then prays that believers will be strengthened through the Holy Spirit.

He wants Jesus to be at home in their hearts through faith.

He asks that they become rooted and established in love and begin to grasp the immeasurable love of Christ.

This love is wider, longer, higher and deeper than we can fully understand.

God is able to do far more than we can ask or imagine through His power at work within us.

His purpose is not merely to gather people into the same room.

It is to form a united family filled with His Presence and love.

Are there cultural, racial or social barriers that still affect how you relate to other believers?

What would it mean for Jesus to be fully at home in every area of your heart?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for bringing me near through the Blood of Jesus.

Thank You that I belong to Your household.

Remove prejudice, hostility and pride from my heart.

Help Your Church live as one family.

Strengthen me through the Holy Spirit.

Root me deeply in the love of Jesus.

May Your Presence be seen among us as You do more than we could ask or imagine.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Reach towards a believer whose background or experience differs from yours.

Choose to listen, welcome and honour them as a member of the same family in Jesus.

steps.title: Walk Worthy of Your Calling
steps.mentor_intro:
The first half of Ephesians explains what God has done for us in Christ.

The second half shows how that truth should change the way we live.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul urges believers to walk in a way that reflects their calling.

Walking is not dramatic.

It means taking one faithful step after another in the right direction.

The first step is humility.

Pride damages unity.

Humility allows us to be patient, gentle and willing to bear with one another in love.

We do not create the unity of the Holy Spirit.

Jesus has already made His people one.

Our responsibility is to protect that unity.

There is one Body.

One Spirit.

One hope.

One Lord.

One faith.

One baptism.

One God and Father of all.

Unity does not mean that every believer has the same gift or function.

Jesus gives different gifts to His Church.

Apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers are given to equip God’s people for service.

Ministry is not reserved for a small group of professionals.

Leaders equip the whole Church so that every believer can serve.

The goal is maturity.

God does not want His people to remain spiritual children, easily carried away by every new teaching.

We grow as we speak the truth in love and remain connected to Jesus, the Head of the Church.

Maturity also requires leaving behind the old way of life.

We put off falsehood and speak truthfully.

We deal with anger before it becomes destructive.

We stop stealing and begin working so that we can share.

We refuse speech that damages people and use words that build them up.

We let go of bitterness, rage, slander and malice.

We become kind, compassionate and forgiving because God has forgiven us in Jesus.

Paul also calls believers to walk in love and light.

Our lives should expose darkness rather than participate in it.

Sexual immorality, greed, impurity and degrading speech do not belong among God’s people.

Instead, we are to understand the Lord’s will and keep being filled with the Holy Spirit.

This filling is not meant to be a single past experience.

We continually depend upon the Holy Spirit.

He fills our worship, gratitude, relationships and daily obedience with the life of Jesus.

Does your daily life reflect the calling you have received from Jesus?

Are your words building people up or contributing to bitterness and division?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Help me walk in a way that honours Your calling.

Remove pride from my heart and teach me to protect the unity of Your Church.

Help me grow into spiritual maturity.

Give me courage to put off the patterns of my old life.

Let my words bring grace and strength to others.

Keep filling me with the Holy Spirit.

Teach me to walk in humility, truth, love and light.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Pay careful attention to your words.

Before speaking, ask whether what you are about to say is true, loving and helpful for building someone up.

steps.title: Stand Firm in the Lord
steps.mentor_intro:
The Gospel transforms our closest relationships.

It also prepares us for a spiritual battle that cannot be fought through human strength.
steps.teaching_content:
Being filled with the Holy Spirit changes the way we treat one another.

Paul begins by calling believers to submit to one another out of reverence for Jesus.

Submission is not permission for control, abuse or domination.

It is the willing choice to place our strength and freedom under the Lordship of Jesus for the good of another person.

Paul applies this to the household.

Wives are called to respect and submit to their husbands as part of their devotion to the Lord.

Husbands receive an even more demanding responsibility.

They must love their wives as Jesus loved the Church and gave Himself for her.

Christian leadership is sacrificial.

It does not demand service.

It gives itself for the good of those entrusted to its care.

Children are called to obey and honour their parents.

Parents must not misuse authority or provoke their children.

They are to raise them with the instruction and character of the Lord.

The principles also reach into working relationships.

Those who work should serve sincerely, remembering that their ultimate Master is Jesus.

Those with authority must treat people fairly, knowing that they too answer to the same Lord.

Paul then turns to spiritual warfare.

Our struggle is not against flesh and blood.

People are not the true enemy.

Behind the visible conflicts are spiritual powers that resist God’s purposes.

We therefore cannot win this battle through anger, manipulation or human strength.

We must become strong in the Lord.

God provides everything needed for us to stand.

Truth holds our lives together.

Righteousness guards our hearts.

The Gospel of peace gives us readiness.

Faith extinguishes the enemy’s attacks.

Salvation protects our minds.

The Word of God becomes the sword of the Holy Spirit.

Prayer keeps us alert and dependent upon God.

The armour provides no encouragement to retreat.

When the battle becomes difficult, we stand.

When lies attack, we stand in truth.

When accusation comes, we stand in the righteousness Jesus provides.

When fear rises, we stand in faith.

When division threatens, we stand in the Gospel of peace.

Victory is not found in focusing constantly on the enemy.

It is found in remaining strong in Jesus and using what God has already provided.

Do your closest relationships reflect the sacrificial character of Jesus?

Are you treating another person as the enemy instead of recognizing the spiritual battle behind the conflict?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Be Lord over my relationships, responsibilities and choices.

Teach me to serve others with humility and love.

Protect every home from control, selfishness and resentment.

Strengthen me for spiritual battle.

Help me stand in truth, righteousness, peace, faith and salvation.

Teach me to use Your Word faithfully and pray continually in the Holy Spirit.

When opposition comes, keep me from retreating.

Make me strong in You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Identify one area in which you have been fighting through anger, fear or human effort.

Place that struggle before Jesus and deliberately respond with truth, prayer and faith.

steps.title: Ephesians: Walk Complete

content.text: lll

You have completed your Walk through Ephesians.

You have seen everything God has given you in Christ.

You have been chosen.

Adopted.

Redeemed.

Forgiven.

Made alive.

Brought near to God.

And sealed with the Holy Spirit.

You are saved by grace through faith.

Not because of the good things you have done, but so that you can walk in the good works God has prepared for you.

Through the Cross, Jesus has broken down the barriers that separated people from God and from one another.

You are no longer an outsider.

You belong to God’s family.

You are part of His Church and a dwelling place for His Presence.

Now continue walking in a way that reflects your calling.

Walk in humility.

Protect the unity of the Holy Spirit.

Grow towards maturity.

Speak the truth in love.

Use your gifts to strengthen others.

Keep being filled with the Holy Spirit.

Let the Lordship of Jesus shape your home, work and relationships.

And when spiritual opposition comes, do not retreat.

Stand firm in the Lord and in His mighty power.

Father,

Thank You for everything You have given me in Jesus.

Thank You for saving me by grace and welcoming me into Your family.

Open the eyes of my heart so that I may continue knowing the hope of Your calling and the greatness of Your power.

Help me walk in humility, unity, maturity, love and purity.

Keep filling me with the Holy Spirit.

Use my gifts to strengthen Your Church.

Let my relationships reflect the sacrificial love of Jesus.

Clothe me with the full Armour of God.

When spiritual opposition comes, help me stand firmly in truth, righteousness, peace, faith and salvation.

May my life bring glory to Jesus and display Your Wisdom to the world.

steps.title: No Other Gospel
steps.mentor_intro:
The believers in Galatia had received the Good News of Jesus.

Then other teachers arrived and began adding requirements to the Gospel.

Paul knew that the truth of the Gospel itself was at stake.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul had brought the Gospel to the cities of Galatia and established new churches there.

After he left, other teachers arrived.

They told the Gentile believers that faith in Jesus was not enough.

If they wanted to belong fully to God’s people, they also needed to be circumcised and keep the Law of Moses.

This sounded spiritual.

It appeared to honour the Old Testament.

But it changed the Gospel.

The message was no longer salvation through Jesus.

It had become Jesus plus religious achievement.

Paul responds with deep concern.

He is astonished that the Galatians are turning so quickly towards a different message.

There is no other Gospel.

Anything that changes the way we are made right with God is not a harmless variation.

It is a distortion of the Good News.

The false teachers also attacked Paul.

They claimed he was not a true apostle and that his message was incomplete.

By undermining the messenger, they hoped to replace his Gospel with their own.

Paul explains that his calling and message did not originate from human beings.

He received the Gospel through a revelation of Jesus Christ.

The man who once tried to destroy the Church had encountered the risen Jesus and been completely transformed.

Paul was not trying to please people.

If pleasing people had been his goal, he would have changed his message to avoid opposition.

But a servant of Jesus must remain faithful to the truth even when it becomes unpopular.

The Church must guard against every “Gospel plus” message.

Jesus plus religious rules.

Jesus plus a particular ceremony.

Jesus plus membership in a certain group.

Jesus plus the approval of a spiritual leader.

Whenever something is added as a requirement for acceptance with God, the Gospel is being changed.

Jesus is not the beginning of salvation while we complete the rest ourselves.

His death and Resurrection are completely sufficient.

We receive salvation through faith in Him.

Nothing needs to be added to Jesus.

Have you ever felt that faith in Jesus was not enough to make you acceptable to God?

Are you more concerned about pleasing people or remaining faithful to the truth of the Gospel?
steps.prayer:
Jesus,

Thank You that Your work is completely sufficient.

Forgive me for the times I have tried to add my own achievements to Your grace.

Protect me from teaching that appears spiritual but draws attention away from You.

Give me discernment to recognize the true Gospel.

Give me courage to remain faithful even when truth is unpopular.

Keep my confidence firmly rooted in You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider whether you have added a personal rule, tradition or achievement to the Good News of Jesus.

Release it and thank Jesus that salvation rests upon what He has done.

steps.title: Justified by Faith
steps.mentor_intro:
A serious conflict arose between Paul and Peter.

The disagreement was not merely about food or culture.

Their behaviour was communicating something false about the Gospel.
steps.teaching_content:
Peter visited the church in Antioch and shared meals with Gentile believers.

He understood that they had been welcomed into God’s family through faith in Jesus.

Then certain Jewish believers arrived.

Peter became afraid of what they might think and began separating himself from the Gentiles.

Other Jewish believers followed his example.

Even Barnabas was influenced.

Peter’s actions suggested that Gentile believers were not fully acceptable unless they adopted Jewish customs.

His behaviour contradicted the Gospel he believed.

Paul confronted him publicly because the truth of the Gospel was at stake.

A person is not justified by keeping the Law.

We are made right with God through faith in Jesus Christ.

Even those born within Israel and raised under the Law had to come to God through Jesus.

If keeping God’s commands could make us right with Him, the death of Jesus would have been unnecessary.

The Law can reveal sin, but it cannot give us the power to become righteous.

It exposes our failure and brings us to the end of self-reliance.

Paul describes the change through the Cross.

He has been crucified with Christ.

His old, self-reliant life no longer controls him.

Jesus now lives in him.

The life Paul continues to live in his body is lived through faith in the Son of God, who loved him and gave Himself for him.

This is not only a truth to understand.

It is a life to live.

We begin with faith in Jesus.

We continue through faith in Jesus.

We do not receive grace and then return to trying to prove ourselves through religious achievement.

The Gospel also changes the way we treat other believers.

If God has welcomed someone through Jesus, we cannot treat them as spiritually inferior because their culture, background or traditions are different from ours.

Peter believed the Gospel.

But fear caused his behaviour to deny it.

We must allow our relationships to reflect the grace we proclaim.

Is there anyone you have treated as less acceptable because their background or traditions differ from yours?

Are you living through faith in Jesus, or have you returned to trying to prove yourself to God?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for making me right with You through faith in Jesus.

Thank You that Jesus loved me and gave Himself for me.

Forgive me for returning to self-reliance and religious performance.

Let the life of Jesus be seen in me.

Give me courage when fear tempts me to compromise the truth.

Teach me to welcome every believer whom You have received through Your grace.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Think about whether fear of people has caused your behaviour to contradict what you believe.

Ask Jesus for the courage to bring your actions back into agreement with the Gospel.

steps.title: Children of the Promise
steps.mentor_intro:
The Galatians began their Christian lives through faith and the power of the Holy Spirit.

Now they were trying to complete their journey through human effort.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul asks the Galatians a direct question.

Did they receive the Holy Spirit by keeping the Law or by believing the Gospel?

They knew the answer.

The Holy Spirit came when they placed their faith in Jesus.

They had begun through the Spirit.

It made no sense to believe that they could now reach maturity through human effort.

Paul points them towards Abraham.

Abraham believed God, and his faith was credited to him as righteousness.

This happened long before the Law of Moses was given.

God promised that all nations would be blessed through Abraham.

That promise finds its fulfilment in Jesus.

Those who belong to Jesus share in the blessing promised to Abraham.

The Law served an important but temporary purpose.

It exposed wrongdoing and restrained sin.

It showed people their need for a Saviour.

It acted like a guardian until Jesus came.

But the Law could not produce the righteousness it required.

If people rely upon keeping the Law, they place themselves under the obligation to obey all of it.

Failure brings judgement.

Jesus rescued us from that curse by taking it upon Himself at the Cross.

Through Him, the blessing promised to Abraham reaches the nations, and we receive the promised Holy Spirit through faith.

Those who trust in Jesus are no longer held under the supervision of the Law.

They have been brought into God’s family.

In Christ, former divisions cannot determine our value or access to God.

Jew and Gentile.

Slave and free.

Male and female.

These differences still exist, but they do not create different levels of acceptance before God.

Everyone who belongs to Jesus is equally included in the promise.

When the right time came, God sent His Son.

Jesus was born under the Law so that He could redeem those under the Law.

Now we receive adoption into God’s family.

We are not slaves trying to earn a place in the household.

We are sons and daughters who have been welcomed by the Father.

The Holy Spirit assures us of this relationship and teaches our hearts to cry out to God as Father.

We do not obey so that we can become His children.

We learn to obey because, through Jesus, He has made us His children.

Are you trying to complete through human effort what God began through the Holy Spirit?

How does knowing that you are God’s child change the way you approach Him?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for the promise fulfilled through Jesus.

Thank You that Jesus carried the curse of sin at the Cross.

Thank You for welcoming me into Your family.

Deliver me from the fear and striving of a slave.

Help me live with the security of Your child.

Fill me with the Holy Spirit.

Teach me to depend upon Your power rather than my own effort.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Approach God as your Father today.

Instead of trying to impress Him, speak honestly and receive the security, guidance and love He gives His children.

steps.title: Freedom Through the Holy Spirit
steps.mentor_intro:
Jesus has set us free.

But Christian freedom is neither a return to religious slavery nor permission to live according to every desire.

It is freedom to walk with the Holy Spirit.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul tells the Galatians to stand firm in the freedom Jesus has given them.

If they accepted circumcision as a requirement for being right with God, they would be placing themselves under the obligation to keep the entire Law.

They would be moving away from grace and returning to slavery.

In Christ, circumcision and uncircumcision do not determine our standing with God.

What matters is faith expressing itself through love.

But freedom can be misunderstood.

Some people use freedom as an excuse to indulge the desires of the flesh.

That is not the freedom Jesus gives.

Jesus frees us from sin so that we can love and serve one another.

The Christian life is not controlled by an external list of rules.

It is directed from within by the Holy Spirit.

The desires of the flesh oppose what the Holy Spirit desires.

The flesh produces behaviour that destroys lives and relationships.

Sexual immorality.

Impurity.

Idolatry.

Hatred.

Jealousy.

Anger.

Selfish ambition.

Division.

Envy.

Drunkenness.

These are not harmless personal choices.

They reveal a life resisting the rule of God.

When the Holy Spirit leads us, He produces a different kind of life.

Love.

Joy.

Peace.

Patience.

Kindness.

Goodness.

Faithfulness.

Gentleness.

Self-control.

This fruit is not produced by trying harder to look religious.

It grows as we remain dependent upon the Holy Spirit.

Those who belong to Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.

That decision must then be worked out in daily life.

We are to keep in step with the Holy Spirit.

He sets the direction.

We follow.

Pride makes us compare ourselves with other people.

It creates rivalry, jealousy and competition.

The Holy Spirit forms a community in which believers serve one another through love.

Christian freedom does not make us independent from everyone.

It frees us to become like Jesus.

Are you more tempted to return to religious rule-keeping or to use freedom as an excuse for compromise?

Which part of the fruit of the Holy Spirit most needs to grow in your life?
steps.prayer:
Holy Spirit,

Thank You for the freedom Jesus has given me.

Keep me from returning to religious slavery.

Keep me from using grace as an excuse for sin.

Lead every part of my life.

Crucify the desires that pull me away from Jesus.

Grow Your fruit within me.

Let love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control become visible in my character.

Help me keep in step with You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Choose one situation in which your natural response is usually anger, impatience, jealousy or selfishness.

Before responding, pause and ask the Holy Spirit to produce the character of Jesus in you.

steps.title: Carry One Another’s Burdens
steps.mentor_intro:
Life in the Holy Spirit changes the way we respond when another believer falls.

We do not ignore sin.

We also do not use someone’s failure as an opportunity to condemn them.

We seek restoration.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul tells spiritually mature believers to restore someone caught in sin.

Restoration must be gentle.

The goal is not humiliation, punishment or gossip.

It is helping a fallen person return to faithful obedience.

Those offering help must remain humble.

They are not beyond temptation.

Spiritual maturity does not look down on the person who has fallen.

It stoops to help them stand again.

Believers are called to carry one another’s burdens.

At the same time, each person must take responsibility for their own life and choices.

These truths belong together.

We are responsible for ourselves.

But we are not expected to walk alone.

Pride prevents both.

It makes us unwilling to admit that we need help.

It also makes us believe we are too important to help someone else.

Paul then gives a principle that applies to every part of life.

We reap what we sow.

If we continually invest in the desires of the flesh, corruption will grow.

If we invest in the things of the Holy Spirit, His life will become increasingly visible.

Our choices matter.

Our habits are seeds.

Words, thoughts, actions, relationships, generosity and obedience all produce a harvest.

Paul encourages believers not to become tired of doing good.

The harvest may not appear immediately.

Faithfulness can feel unnoticed.

Serving others can become exhausting.

But a harvest will come if we do not give up.

Therefore, whenever God gives us an opportunity, we should do good to others, especially to fellow believers.

Paul ends where the Christian life always returns.

The Cross.

The false teachers wanted to boast about outward religious marks and the number of people they had persuaded to join their system.

Paul would boast only in the Cross of Jesus Christ.

Through the Cross, the old world had lost its hold upon him.

Religious status could not save anyone.

What matters is becoming a new creation.

The Christian life is not about adding religion to the old self.

It is about Jesus making us new from within.

When another believer fails, is your first response restoration, judgement or gossip?

What are you presently sowing through your repeated choices and habits?
steps.prayer:
Father,

Thank You for making me new through Jesus.

Give me a gentle and humble heart towards people who have fallen.

Help me carry the burdens of others without ignoring my own responsibilities.

Show me what I am sowing through my daily choices.

Give me strength not to become tired of doing good.

Keep me from boasting in appearance, achievement or religious performance.

May my only confidence be in the Cross of Jesus Christ.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Look for an opportunity to help carry someone’s burden.

Respond gently, practically and without drawing attention to yourself.

content.text:

We are justified through faith in Jesus Christ.

Jesus loved us and gave Himself for us.

At the Cross, He carried the curse of sin and opened the way for us to become children of God.

You are not a slave trying to earn a place in God’s household.

Through Jesus, you have been welcomed into His family.

The Holy Spirit assures you that you belong to the Father.

It is freedom to love.

Freedom to serve.

Freedom to become more like Jesus.

Continue walking with the Holy Spirit.

Allow Him to grow love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control within you.

Carry the burdens of others.

Restore those who fall with gentleness.

Do not become tired of doing good.

And never place your confidence in outward appearance or religious performance.

Boast only in the Cross of Jesus Christ.

steps.title: God Came to Us

content.text:
We ended the last Walk with a problem.

Humanity had turned away from God.

Sin had damaged the relationship we were created to have with Him.

And we couldn't rescue ourselves.

So what did God do?

He came to us.

John begins his Gospel in an unusual way.

He doesn't begin with Jesus being born in Bethlehem.

He takes us much further back.

"In the beginning..."

We've heard those words before.

Genesis begins the same way.

John tells us that before Jesus was born, He already existed.

He calls Jesus "the Word."

The Word was with God.

The Word was God.

And then John says something extraordinary:

"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us."

**God came to us.**

Jesus wasn't simply another prophet pointing people toward God.

He wasn't merely a wise teacher with good ideas.

In Jesus, God entered our world.

Think about what that means.

Humanity had turned away from God.

We had chosen our own way.

We had damaged the relationship God created us to enjoy.

If anyone had the right to walk away, it was God.

But He didn't.

Instead of waiting for humanity to somehow climb its way back to Him, God stepped into our broken world.

Jesus experienced hunger.

Tiredness.

Friendship.

Rejection.

Grief.

Pain.

Temptation.

He walked among ordinary people.

He touched people others avoided.

He welcomed people others rejected.

He showed compassion to the hurting.

He confronted hypocrisy.

He forgave sinners.

And through it all, He showed us what God is like.

Remember where our journey began?

We asked:

Who is God?

Jesus brings that question remarkably close.

If you want to know what God is like, look at Jesus.

But Jesus didn't come only to show us God.

He came because we needed to be saved.

And that would eventually take Him to the Cross.

Jesus, help me to understand who You really are.

Thank You that You didn't remain distant from our broken world.

Thank You for coming to us.

As I learn more about You, show me what You reveal about God and help me understand why You came.

Amen.

Spend some time considering this truth:

God came to us.

Christianity isn't primarily the story of people searching until they finally find God.

It is the story of God coming to find us.

Ask yourself:

What does that tell me about the kind of God He is?

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
We couldn't reach our way back to God.

So God came to us.
content.lookingAhead:
Jesus came into our world for a reason.

He knew where His journey would eventually lead.

The cross wasn't an accident.

Tomorrow we'll discover why Jesus was willing to take our place.

steps.title: Jesus Took Our Place

content.text:
Jesus came to show us what God is like.

But He came for something more.

Humanity had a problem we couldn't solve.

Sin had consequences we couldn't undo.

Jesus came to do for us what we could never do for ourselves.

The Cross is probably the most recognisable symbol of Christianity.

We see it on churches.

People wear it around their necks.

It appears in Christian art.

But why is an instrument of execution at the centre of the Christian faith?

Because Christians believe something extraordinary happened there.

Jesus wasn't simply the victim of a tragic execution.

Peter tells us:

"He himself bore our sins in his body on the cross."

Jesus took our place.

We've already discovered that sin separates us from God and that sin has consequences.

God is loving, but He is also holy and just.

He doesn't pretend evil doesn't matter.

Our sin couldn't simply be ignored.

And we couldn't undo it ourselves.

So Jesus did something we could never do.

He carried our sin.

Think about the significance of that.

The One who had no sin took upon Himself the consequences of ours.

The guilty were offered forgiveness because the innocent One took their place.

This is why the cross is such good news.

Jesus didn't stand at a distance and tell broken humanity to try harder.

He stepped into our place.

The cross tells us how seriously God takes sin.

But it also tells us how far God was willing to go to save us.

Jesus willingly gave Himself for us.

For the things we're ashamed of.

For the choices we wish we could undo.

For the sin nobody else knows about.

For all the ways we've chosen our way instead of God's.

Jesus carried our sin to the cross.

Jesus, thank You for what You did for me.

Help me to understand the significance of the Cross.

Thank You for taking upon Yourself what I could never remove by my own effort.

Help me not to hide from my sin or minimise it, but to understand the forgiveness You came to make possible.

Amen.

Think about the Cross differently today.

Don't see it merely as a Christian symbol.

Remember what it represents:

Jesus took our place.

If there are things in your life that fill you with guilt or shame, bring them honestly to God.

You don't have to hide.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
At the Cross, Jesus took upon Himself what belonged to us.

He took our place.
content.lookingAhead:
But why would Jesus do this?

Why would God go to such extraordinary lengths for people who had turned away from Him?

Tomorrow we'll discover what the cross reveals about the heart of God.

steps.title: The Price Was Paid

content.text:
The cross shows us the seriousness of sin.

But it also reveals something else.

Something we've been discovering from the beginning of this journey.

God loves us.

Sometimes we imagine that God will love us once we've become better people.

Once we've stopped making mistakes.

Once we've sorted ourselves out.

Once we're good enough.

But Paul tells the story very differently.

He says:

"While we were still sinners, Christ died for us."

Not after we fixed ourselves.

Not after we earned God's attention.

Not after we became religious.

While we were still sinners.

Jesus died for us.

The Cross brings together truths about God that we've already discovered.

God is holy.

Sin matters to Him.

God is just.

Wrong cannot simply be declared unimportant.

But God is also loving.

And rather than leaving us to bear the consequences of our rebellion alone, God acted to save us.

This is grace.

God giving us what we could never earn.

At the cross, Jesus paid the price for our sin.

Forgiveness isn't God pretending our sin never mattered.

It cost something.

It cost Jesus His life.

That should keep us from treating sin lightly.

But it should also keep us from believing that our sin is greater than God's willingness to forgive.

Maybe you've thought:

"God could never forgive what I've done."

The Cross says otherwise.

God already knew the worst about humanity when Jesus came.

He knew our selfishness.

Our rebellion.

Our secrets.

Our failures.

And still:

Christ died for us.

The Cross isn't evidence that we were good enough for God.

It's evidence that God loved us when we weren't.

God, thank You for loving me before I could ever earn it.

Thank You that Jesus gave His life for me while I was still a sinner.

Help me to understand both the seriousness of my sin and the greatness of Your grace.

Where I carry guilt and believe I am beyond forgiveness, help me to look again at the Cross.

Amen.

Consider these words:

"While we were still sinners, Christ died for us."

What would change if you genuinely believed that God's love isn't something you have to earn?

Bring whatever comes to mind honestly to Him.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
The Cross doesn't tell us how worthy we were.

It tells us how deeply God loved us.
content.lookingAhead:
Jesus died.

His body was placed in a tomb.

For His followers, it looked like everything was over.

But the Christian message doesn't end with a dead Saviour.

Tomorrow we come to the moment that changes everything:

**Jesus is alive.**

steps.title: Jesus Is Alive

content.text:
Jesus was crucified.

He died.

He was buried.

If the story ended there, Christianity would have no good news to announce.

But on the third day, something happened that changed everything.

Jesus rose from the dead.

The resurrection isn't an optional extra added to the story of Jesus.

It stands at the centre of the Christian faith.

Paul summarises the message he received and passed on:

Christ died for our sins.

He was buried.

He was raised on the third day.

Jesus is alive.

The Cross looked like defeat.

The resurrection revealed victory.

Sin had brought death into God's good creation.

Jesus entered death—and came out the other side.

Death did not have the final word.

The resurrection tells us that Jesus really is who He claimed to be.

It tells us that His work at the Cross was not a failure.

It tells us that death itself has been confronted.

And it gives followers of Jesus hope that reaches beyond this life.

Christianity isn't built around the memory of a great teacher who lived long ago.

Christians worship a living Saviour.

That changes everything.

Jesus isn't simply someone whose teachings we study.

He is Someone we can know.

The same Jesus who welcomed broken people, forgave sinners, touched the rejected and gave His life on the Cross is alive.

And because He lives, the invitation to know Him is still open.

The resurrection also tells us something about our own brokenness.

God isn't merely interested in helping us manage the old life.

Jesus came to bring new life.

The story that began with creation, was damaged by sin and seemed to end at a Cross suddenly bursts open with hope.

God is making things new.

Jesus, thank You that death did not defeat You.

Thank You that You are alive.

Help me to understand what Your resurrection means.

Give me hope where I have believed that brokenness, failure or even death must have the final word.

Help me to know You not merely as someone from history, but as the Living Saviour.

Amen.

Consider the difference between these two statements:

Jesus lived.

Jesus lives.

Christianity makes the second claim.

Ask yourself:

If Jesus really is alive, what might that mean for my life?

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
The Cross wasn't the end.

The tomb wasn't the end.

Jesus is alive.
content.lookingAhead:
Jesus came.

Jesus died for our sins.

Jesus rose again.

But knowing that happened isn't quite the same as receiving what He offers.

Tomorrow the story becomes personal.

What will you do with Jesus?

The same Jesus who welcomed broken people, forgave sinners, touched the rejected and gave His life on the Cross is alive.

And because He lives, the invitation to know Him is still open.

The resurrection also tells us something about our own brokenness.

God isn't merely interested in helping us manage the old life.

Jesus came to bring new life.

The story that began with creation, was damaged by sin and seemed to end at a Cross suddenly bursts open with hope.

God is making things new.
steps.prayer:
Jesus, thank You that death did not defeat You.

Thank You that You are alive.

Help me to understand what Your resurrection means.

Give me hope where I have believed that brokenness, failure or even death must have the final word.

Help me to know You not merely as someone from history, but as the Living Saviour.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider the difference between these two statements:

Jesus lived.

Jesus lives.

Christianity makes the second claim.

Ask yourself:

If Jesus really is alive, what might that mean for my life?

steps.title: The Gift Is Offered to You

content.text:
We've discovered who Jesus is.

We've seen why He came.

We've stood at the Cross.

We've looked into the empty tomb.

Now we come to a deeply personal question.

What does any of this mean for you?

Most of us understand earning.

You work and receive a salary.

You study and earn a qualification.

You train and improve.

You perform well and receive recognition.

So it's easy to carry the same thinking into our relationship with God.

Maybe if I become good enough...

Maybe if I go to church enough...

Maybe if I pray enough...

Maybe if I stop doing certain things...

Then perhaps God will accept me.

But the gospel turns that thinking upside down.

Paul says:

"It is by grace you have been saved, through faith."

Then he makes it unmistakably clear:

"This is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works."

Salvation is a gift.

You don't earn a gift.

You receive it.

Jesus has already done what you could never do for yourself.

He came to us.

He took our sin upon Himself.

He died.

He rose again.

And now God offers forgiveness and new life.

The Bible calls us to respond with repentance and faith.

Repentance means turning.

It means recognising that we've been living our own way and turning toward God.

Faith means trust.

Not simply believing that Jesus existed.

Not merely agreeing with Christian information.

It means placing your trust in Jesus and what He has done for you.

Perhaps you've followed these Walks because you're curious.

Perhaps you've been around Christianity your entire life.

Perhaps you're only beginning to realise that knowing about Jesus isn't the same as trusting Him.

Wherever you are, Jesus' invitation is personal.

You don't need to clean yourself up before coming to Him.

You don't need to become religious enough.

You don't need to pretend you have no doubts or questions.

You can come honestly.

Salvation isn't a reward for people who finally become good enough.

It is God's gift to people who know they need a Saviour.

Jesus, I recognise that I cannot save myself.

I have sinned and chosen my own way.

Thank You for coming for me.

Thank You for taking my sin to the Cross.

Thank You for dying and rising again.

I turn from living life only on my own terms and place my trust in You.

Forgive me.

Lead me.

Teach me to know You and to follow You.

Thank You for offering me the gift of new life.

I accept You as my Lord and Saviour.

Amen.

Don't rush past this moment.

Ask yourself honestly:

Am I trusting Jesus—or do I simply know things about Him?

If you're ready to trust Him, talk to Him.

There isn't a magic formula of words you have to repeat.

Come honestly.

Acknowledge your need for Him.

Turn toward Him.

Trust what He has done for you.

And if you still have questions, keep walking.

Jesus isn't frightened by honest questions.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You couldn't rescue yourself.

You didn't have to.

Jesus came to rescue you.

It's the beginning of a new one.

What happens now?

How do you begin walking with Jesus?

What changes?

How do you grow?

That's where we're going next:

Beginning Your New Life.

steps.title: Jesus Saves

content.text:
You've completed Jesus Saves.

Everything in this Journey has been leading to what you've just discovered.

God created you.

You were made in His image.

Humanity turned away from God and sin damaged the relationship we were created to have with Him.

We couldn't repair that relationship ourselves.

So God came to us.

Jesus entered our broken world.

He took our sin upon Himself at the Cross.

He gave His life for us.

And on the third day, He rose again.

Jesus is alive.

The heart of the Christian message isn't that you need to become good enough for God.

It's that Jesus has already done what you could never do for yourself.

Salvation is God's gift.

Grace means you don't earn it.

Faith means you trust Him.

Repentance means you turn from living life your own way and turn toward Him.

And when you come to Jesus, you're not coming to someone who reluctantly tolerates you.

You're coming to the One who loved you enough to give His life for you.

Maybe during this Walk you've chosen to place your trust in Jesus for the first time.

Maybe you've followed Him for years and have been reminded again of what He has done for you.

Or perhaps you still have questions.

Wherever you are, keep walking.

Because Jesus didn't only come to forgive your past.

He came to give you new life.

And that life with Him is only beginning.
