steps.title: When We Chose Our Own Way

content.closingText: Sin begins when we stop trusting God's way and choose our own.
content.lookingAhead:
Adam and Eve got what they chose.

They stepped outside God's way.

But instead of finding greater freedom, something happened immediately.

They hid.

Tomorrow we'll discover one of sin's deepest consequences:

It separates us from God.

steps.mentor_intro:
Yesterday we saw that God gave humanity freedom, responsibility and a boundary.

At the heart of that boundary was a question:

Will you trust God?

Today another voice enters the story.

A voice that suggests that perhaps God cannot be trusted after all.
steps.teaching_content:
The serpent's first attack wasn't really against the fruit.

It was against God's character.

"Did God really say...?"

Then came the suggestion that God was withholding something good from Adam and Eve.

Suddenly the God who had created them, provided for them and walked with them was being presented as someone who couldn't be trusted.

Adam and Eve faced a choice.

Would they trust what God had said?

Or would they decide for themselves what was good?

They chose their own way.

That is the heart of what the Bible calls sin.

We often think of sin simply as doing bad things.

Lying.

Stealing.

Hurting someone.

Sexual immorality.

Greed.

Hatred.

Those things matter.

But underneath them is something deeper.

Sin says:

"I will decide what is right for me."

"I will live life on my terms."

"I know better than God."

That's what happened in the garden.

Human beings who were created to live under God's loving rule chose independence from Him.

And we recognise that same desire in ourselves.

We may want God when we need help.

We may want His protection, His provision and His blessing.

But when His way conflicts with ours, something inside us often says:

"I want to decide."

Adam and Eve ate the fruit.

It may have seemed like one small act.

But behind that act was a devastating decision.

Humanity chose life on its own terms instead of trusting its Creator.

And everything changed.
steps.prayer:
God, I recognise that I often want to do things my own way.

Forgive me for the times I've distrusted Your goodness and believed that I know better than You.

Help me to recognise sin not only in the obvious things I do wrong, but also in the places where my heart turns away from You.

Teach me to trust You.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider this question:

Where in my life am I most tempted to say, "I know better than God"?

You don't need to defend your answer or make excuses.

Simply be honest with God about it.

steps.title: Sin Separates Us from God

content.closingText:
Sin makes us want to hide from God.

But God is still the One who comes looking for us.
content.lookingAhead:
The damage didn't remain inside the garden.

Sin spread.

Through humanity.

Through relationships.

Through our world.

And through every one of us.

Tomorrow we'll look honestly at the broken world we now live in.

steps.mentor_intro:
Adam and Eve had chosen their own way.

Then they heard God approaching.

Once, God's presence had meant relationship.

Now they did something they had never needed to do before.

They hid.
steps.teaching_content:
There is something heartbreaking about this moment.

God comes into the garden.

And Adam and Eve hide from Him.

The people created to know God are now afraid of Him.

Something has broken.

Sin doesn't only cause us to do things we regret.

It damages the relationship we were created to have with God.

Adam tells God:

"I was afraid... so I hid."

We still do this.

When we know we've done something wrong, our instinct is often to hide.

We avoid the person we've hurt.

We cover things up.

We make excuses.

We blame someone else.

And sometimes we hide from God.

We stop praying.

We avoid Scripture.

We stay away from church.

We tell ourselves we'll come back to God once we've sorted ourselves out.

But notice something important in Genesis.

Adam and Eve are hiding.

God is the One who comes looking.

"Where are you?"

God wasn't asking because He had lost Adam.

He was drawing Adam out of hiding.

Sin creates separation, shame and fear.

But even in this first moment of human failure, God moves toward broken humanity.

That doesn't make sin unimportant.

There will be consequences.

But it reveals something about God.

Humanity runs.

God seeks.

That pattern will become increasingly important as the biblical story unfolds.
steps.prayer:
God, You already know the things I would rather hide.

Help me to stop running from You.

Give me courage to be honest about my failures and the places where I've chosen my own way.

Thank You that even when humanity hid from You, You came looking.

Help me to come into Your presence honestly.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Is there something you're hiding from God?

Perhaps something you've done.

Something you're ashamed of.

Something you're afraid to face.

Instead of hiding it, talk to God honestly about it.

He already knows.

steps.title: A Broken World

content.closingText:
The brokenness of our world isn't only around us.

It runs through us.
content.lookingAhead:
If everyone has sinned...

If sin separates us from God...

And if we cannot repair the problem ourselves...

Then we face an unavoidable question:

Who can rescue us?

steps.mentor_intro:
It's easy to look at the world and see what's wrong with it.

Violence.

Greed.

Injustice.

Hatred.

Broken families.

Abuse.

Corruption.

But the Bible makes the problem uncomfortable.

Sin isn't only something other people do.

It reaches every one of us.
steps.teaching_content:
Paul writes:

"All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God."

All.

Not some.

Not only terrible people.

Not only criminals.

Not only people whose failures are obvious.

All of us.

Remember what we discovered in the previous Walk.

Human beings were created in God's image and intended to reflect His character.

But when we look honestly at ourselves, none of us reflects Him perfectly.

We lie.

We become selfish.

We hurt people.

We envy.

We judge.

We hold grudges.

We put ourselves first.

Sometimes our sin is visible to everyone.

Sometimes nobody else knows.

But God does.

This is one of the difficult truths of Christianity:

The problem with the world isn't only "those people."

The problem runs through humanity.

Including us.

Sin has affected our relationship with God.

Our relationship with one another.

Our relationship with ourselves.

Even creation itself bears the consequences of humanity's rebellion.

This explains something about the world we experience.

The Bible doesn't pretend everything is fine.

It tells us that the world we know isn't the world as God originally intended it to be.

Something is broken.

And if we're part of the problem, then simply telling humanity to try harder isn't enough.

We need something more.
steps.prayer:
God, it's easy for me to see what is wrong in other people.

Help me to be honest about myself.

Show me where my thoughts, attitudes, words and actions fall short of Your ways.

Keep me from judging others while ignoring my own need for You.

Help me to understand how deeply humanity needs Your help.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Instead of thinking about someone else's failures today, ask:

Where do I fall short of God's character?

Don't use the answer to condemn yourself.

Use it to become honest with God.

steps.title: We Need a Rescuer

content.closingText:
Our sin is real.

Our separation from God is real.

But neither gets the final word.
content.lookingAhead:
We began this Walk asking:

What went wrong?

Now we know.

Humanity turned away from God and chose its own way.

But God didn't turn away from us.

Next we're going to discover the heart of the Christian message.

Why did Jesus come?

Why did He die?

What happened at the cross?

And can what Jesus did really change your story?

Next:

Jesus Saves.

steps.mentor_intro:
We've reached the difficult truth at the centre of this Walk.

Humanity chose its own way.

Sin entered God's good creation.

Our relationship with God was broken.

And none of us has escaped the problem.

So what now?
steps.teaching_content:
Paul puts the situation plainly:

"The wages of sin is death..."

Sin has consequences.

Separation from the God who gives life ultimately leads to death.

That's the seriousness of the problem.

We cannot solve it simply by becoming a little more religious.

We cannot erase our past by doing enough good things.

We cannot repair our relationship with God through our own effort.

If the problem were simply that we lacked information, we would need a teacher.

If the problem were simply that we needed better habits, we would need a coach.

If the problem were simply that society needed improvement, we would need reform.

But the Bible says our problem goes much deeper.

We need to be rescued.

And then Romans 6:23 changes direction.

"The wages of sin is death, but..."

That word matters.

But.

Human failure isn't the end of God's story.

We chose to turn away from God.

God did not choose to abandon us.

The verse continues by speaking about God's gift of eternal life through Jesus Christ.

We're going to spend the next Walk discovering what that means.

For now, understand this:

Christianity isn't the story of humanity finding a way to climb back to God.

It's the story of God coming to rescue humanity.

We needed a Rescuer.

And God sent One.
steps.prayer:
God, I recognise that I cannot fix everything that is broken in me.

I cannot erase my sin or restore my relationship with You through my own effort.

Thank You that You didn't abandon humanity when we turned away from You.

Help me to understand the rescue You have provided.

And help me to discover who Jesus really is and what He has done for me.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Consider this question:

Have I been trying to make myself good enough for God?

You don't have to solve the problem today.

Simply acknowledge your need.

Sometimes the first step toward being rescued is admitting:

I cannot rescue myself.

steps.title: There Is Hope

content.text:
You've completed What Went Wrong?

This hasn't been the easiest part of the journey.

We've looked honestly at something we'd often rather avoid.

God created humanity in His image, with purpose, value and the freedom to trust Him.

But humanity chose another way.

And we still do.

Sin is more than a collection of bad things people do. At its heart, sin is our decision to live our way instead of God's way.

It damages our relationship with God.

It damages our relationships with one another.

And its effects can be seen throughout our broken world.

But perhaps the most important discovery you've made is this:

We cannot rescue ourselves.

Trying harder cannot erase our sin.

Being religious cannot repair the separation.

Doing good things cannot undo everything we've done wrong.

We need someone to rescue us.

And that's where the story changes.

Because God didn't look at broken humanity and walk away.

He came for us.

The bad news helps us understand why the good news is so extraordinary.

And now we're ready to discover it.

God created humanity in His image, with purpose, value and the freedom to trust Him.

But humanity chose another way.

And we still do.

Sin is more than a collection of bad things people do. At its heart, sin is our decision to live our way instead of God's way.

It damages our relationship with God.

It damages our relationships with one another.

And its effects can be seen throughout our broken world.

But perhaps the most important discovery you've made is this:

We cannot rescue ourselves.

Trying harder cannot erase our sin.

Being religious cannot repair the separation.

Doing good things cannot undo everything we've done wrong.

We need someone to rescue us.

And that's where the story changes.

Because God didn't look at broken humanity and walk away.

He came for us.

The bad news helps us understand why the good news is so extraordinary.

And now we're ready to discover it.

steps.title: God Wants to Be Known

content.text:
Good to have you here.

We're beginning with one of the biggest questions anyone can ask:

Who is God?

People have answered that question in countless ways. But instead of beginning with our ideas about God, let's begin with what God has revealed about Himself.

The remarkable thing about the God of the Bible isn't simply that He exists.

It's that He wants to be known.

God could have remained distant and mysterious. Instead, He has made Himself known.

We see something of Him in creation. We discover His character and His ways throughout Scripture. And ultimately, God makes Himself known to us through Jesus.

That changes the question.

Instead of only asking, "Is there a God?" we can begin asking:

"What is God like?"

"Can I know Him?"

"Does He know me?"

Jeremiah tells us that there are many things people can build their lives around—wisdom, strength, wealth and achievement. None of them are necessarily wrong.

But God says there is something greater:

Knowing Him.

Christianity isn't primarily an invitation to learn religious information.

It's an invitation to know God.

You may have known about God for years without ever thinking that you could actually know Him.

Or perhaps you're only beginning to explore whether you believe in God at all.

Either way, you don't have to pretend.

You can begin right where you are.

The God we're going to discover throughout this Walk isn't asking you to understand everything about Him before you come closer.

He's inviting you to know Him.

God, I want to know You as You really are, not simply as I have imagined You to be.

As I begin this journey, help me to understand what You have revealed about Yourself.

Give me an open heart and help me to recognise You.

Amen.

Think about this question today:

When I think about God, what do I believe He is like?

Don't try to give the "right" Christian answer.

Simply be honest.

As we continue this Walk, allow what Scripture reveals about God to shape—or even challenge—the picture you already have of Him.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You don't need to know everything about God to begin knowing Him.

You just need to be willing to come and see.
content.lookingAhead:
Next, we're going right back to the beginning.

Before there was you, me, the earth or anything we can see, God was already there.

We'll discover what it means to call Him Creator.

steps.title: God the Creator

content.text:
Yesterday we began with the truth that God wants to be known.

Today we're going back to the opening words of the Bible.

Before we learn what God has done for us, we need to understand something fundamental about who He is.

He is the Creator.

The Bible begins with a remarkable statement:

"In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth."

Before the earth existed, God was there.

Before the oceans, mountains and stars existed, God was there.

Before humanity existed, God was there.

Everything we see around us ultimately begins with Him.

Genesis shows us a God who doesn't create randomly or without purpose. There is order and intention in what He does.

Light.

Sky.

Land and sea.

Plants and trees.

Sun, moon and stars.

Living creatures.

And eventually, humanity.

Creation reveals something about its Creator.

Think about the extraordinary complexity of the world around us. From the vastness of the universe to the smallest details of life, creation points beyond itself to the greatness, wisdom and power of God.

God is not simply part of creation.

He is its Architect.

And because He created it, He is also its rightful Ruler.

That has an important implication for us.

If God is our Creator, then our lives aren't meaningless accidents.

There is purpose behind our existence.

We haven't yet reached the question of why God created you. We'll explore that in the next Walk, Created in God's Image.

For now, simply allow this truth to settle:

The God who wants you to know Him is the same God who created everything.

And yet this great God chooses to make Himself known to us.

God, You are the Creator of heaven and earth.

Everything exists because of You.

Help me to see Your greatness in what You have made and to understand more clearly who You are.

As I continue this journey, teach me to see my life and the world around me from Your perspective.

Amen.

Take notice of the world around you today.

Something ordinary may catch your attention—the sky, a tree, the ocean, another person, or simply the complexity of life.

Allow it to remind you:

This world has a Creator.

And then consider what creation might be telling you about Him.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
Creation is extraordinary.

But the One who created it is greater still.
content.lookingAhead:
Knowing that God created everything tells us something about His power.

But what is this Creator actually like?

Next we'll begin discovering the character of God—His holiness, goodness, faithfulness, justice and mercy.

steps.title: What Is God Like?

content.text:
Knowing that God created everything tells us that He is powerful.

But it doesn't answer another important question:

What is God actually like?

The Bible doesn't leave us to guess.

Again and again, God reveals His character to us.

If someone asked you to describe God, what words would you use?

Powerful?

Strict?

Distant?

Kind?

Angry?

Loving?

Sometimes our picture of God has been shaped more by our experiences, our upbringing, other people, or even bad experiences of religion than by God Himself.

That's why this moment in Exodus is so important.

Moses asks to see God's glory. And when God reveals Himself, He doesn't only demonstrate His power.

He describes His character.

He is compassionate.

He is gracious.

He is patient.

He is filled with love.

He is faithful.

He forgives.

But God also says that He does not simply ignore wrongdoing.

That matters.

God isn't loving instead of being just.

And He isn't holy instead of being compassionate.

Everything that is true about God belongs together.

God is holy.

There is no evil or corruption in Him.

God is just.

He cares about what is right and wrong.

God is merciful.

He doesn't treat broken people as though they are beyond hope.

God is faithful.

He can be trusted.

God is good.

His character doesn't change according to His mood or circumstances.

And God is loving.

As we continue through Emmaus, we'll discover each of these truths more deeply.

For now, there's something important to understand:

We don't get to create God in the image we would prefer.

We allow God to reveal Himself to us.

And the more we discover who He really is, the more we realise that He is worthy of our trust.

God, sometimes my understanding of You has been shaped by things other than You.

Help me to know You as You really are.

Show me Your character through Your Word.

Help me to trust Your goodness, Your holiness, Your justice, Your mercy and Your faithfulness.

Amen.

Consider this honestly:

What has shaped my picture of God?

Perhaps it was your family.

Church.

Something someone taught you.

Something painful that happened.

Or perhaps you've simply never thought much about Him before.

As you continue this journey, be willing to allow God to show you through Scripture who He really is.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You don't have to invent a picture of God.

He has chosen to reveal Himself.
content.lookingAhead:
We've discovered that God is holy, good, just, merciful and faithful.

But Scripture reveals something else that brings the character of God remarkably close to us:

God is love.

Next we'll explore what that means—and what God's love has to do with you personally.

steps.title: God Is Love

content.text:
We've seen that God is Creator.

We've begun discovering His character—holy, just, merciful, good and faithful.

Today we come to something at the very heart of who God is:

God is love.

And His love isn't merely something the Bible asks us to believe.

God has shown us what His love looks like.

We use the word love for all sorts of things.

We love people.

We love food.

We love music.

We love places and experiences.

But when the Bible tells us that God is love, it is saying something far deeper.

Love isn't simply something God occasionally does.

Love is part of who He is.

And God doesn't merely tell us that He loves us.

He demonstrates it.

John says that God showed His love by sending His Son into the world so that we might have life through Him.

That's important because it means God's love doesn't depend upon us earning it.

You don't have to become good enough for God to start loving you.

You don't have to clean up your life first.

You don't have to impress Him.

God's love begins with God, not with our performance.

But God's love also doesn't mean that He simply ignores everything that's wrong with us or with our world.

Remember what we've already discovered.

God is loving and holy.

God is merciful and just.

That's why Jesus is so important.

At the cross, we begin to see God's holiness, justice, mercy and love coming together.

We'll explore that much more deeply when we reach the Walk Jesus Saves.

For now, don't rush past this:

The Creator of everything loves you.

Not because you've earned His love.

Not because you've managed to get everything right.

He loves because love is part of who He is.

Perhaps your experience of human love has made that difficult to believe.

People can love us one day and reject us the next.

People disappoint us.

Sometimes the people who were supposed to love us have hurt us deeply.

God's love isn't like that.

His love is rooted in His character.

And that means you can begin learning to trust it.

God, thank You that Your love doesn't depend upon me earning it.

Help me to understand what Your love is really like.

Where my experiences have given me a distorted picture of love, show me the difference between imperfect human love and Your faithful love.

Help me to receive Your love and to trust You more.

Amen.

Consider this question:

Do I find it easy or difficult to believe that God loves me?

Be honest about your answer.

You don't need to force yourself to feel anything.

Simply bring your answer to God and allow Him to continue showing you what His love is like.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
God doesn't merely say that He loves.

He has shown us.

And the clearest picture of that love is Jesus.
content.lookingAhead:
We've spent these first days discovering things about God.

But Christianity doesn't end with knowing facts about Him.

Tomorrow we'll bring the Walk to its most important question:

Can I actually know God?

And we'll discover that His invitation isn't simply to learn more about Him.

It's to walk with Him.

steps.title: Knowing God

content.text:
Over the past few days we've been asking:

Who is God?

We've discovered some important answers.

But today we come to something even more important.

God doesn't only want you to know things about Him.

He invites you to know Him.

There's a big difference between knowing about someone and actually knowing them.

You can know someone's name.

You can know where they were born.

You can know what they've accomplished.

You might even know what they believe.

And still not know them personally.

The same can be true of God.

It's possible to know Bible stories, attend church, understand Christian beliefs and use Christian language—and still experience God mainly as someone you've heard about.

Jesus describes something much deeper.

He says that eternal life is to know God and to know Jesus Christ whom He sent.

That's extraordinary.

The God who created everything isn't simply looking for people who can answer questions about Him correctly.

He invites us into relationship with Him.

Throughout this Walk we've discovered that God has made Himself known.

We've seen that He is Creator.

We've begun exploring His character.

We've discovered that He loves us.

But knowing God is a journey.

You won't understand everything about Him after five days.

None of us ever will.

Relationships grow as people spend time together. We listen. We speak. We learn to trust. We discover more of who the other person is.

Our relationship with God grows too.

We learn to hear Him through Scripture.

We speak to Him in prayer.

We learn to trust Him.

We begin allowing Him to shape the way we live.

And most importantly, we discover God through Jesus.

Jesus doesn't merely teach us things about God.

He shows us what God is like and makes it possible for us to come to Him.

There is much more of that story ahead.

For now, perhaps the most important question isn't:

"How much do I know about God?"

Perhaps it's:

"Do I want to know Him?"

If your answer is yes—even if you still have questions—that is a wonderful place to begin.

God, thank You for making Yourself known.

I don't want simply to know things about You. I want to know You.

Help me to discover who You really are.

Teach me through Your Word.

Help me to recognise Your presence, trust Your character and understand more of Your love.

And as I continue this journey, lead me closer to Jesus.

Amen.

Take what may be a very simple step.

Talk to God.

You don't need special words or religious language.

Tell Him honestly where you are.

You might have faith.

You might have doubts.

You might have questions.

You might simply be curious.

Whatever is true, bring that to Him.

Knowing God begins with coming to Him honestly.

content.message: Well done! You have completed today's reading.

content.closingText:
You began this Walk with a question:

Who is God?

There is much more to discover.

But now you know something remarkable about the answer:

The God you're searching for wants to be known.
content.lookingAhead:

Now the journey turns toward another important question:

Who are you?

Why did God create humanity?

Is there purpose behind your life?

And what does the Bible mean when it says that human beings were created in the image of God?

That's where we're going next.

steps.title: You’ve Begun to Know Him!

content.text:
You began this Walk with one of life's biggest questions:

Who is God?

You've discovered that God wants to be known.

He is the Creator of everything. He is holy, good, just, merciful and faithful. And remarkably, this great God is also a God of love.

But perhaps the most important discovery is that God doesn't simply invite you to learn more about Him.

He invites you to know Him.

Five days haven't answered every question about God—and they were never meant to.

This is only the beginning.

Keep asking questions. Keep opening Scripture. Keep talking to God. Keep discovering who He is.

There is so much more ahead.

Amen.

Five days haven't answered every question about God—and they were never meant to.

This is only the beginning.

Keep asking questions. Keep opening Scripture. Keep talking to God. Keep discovering who He is.

There is so much more ahead.
steps.prayer:
God, thank You for what You have shown me about Yourself.

Thank You that You are not distant or unknowable, but that You have chosen to make Yourself known.

Help me to keep seeking You, learning from Your Word and growing in my understanding of who You are.

As I continue this journey, show me more of who You are—and help me understand who You created me to be.

Amen.
